Input: I will update this as i have more information.

For now, i can only rate the company itself. The seeds arrived promptly and were well protected. They came with complete instructions for successful planting, which many seeds dont. The seeds themselves are pea sized and furry looking. In fact, they almost look like tiny candy corns.

For now, i am in the midst of stage one, which is to refrigerate the seeds for 14 days. I put them in on June 13th. On June 27th, i will continue on with the planting process and will update this review then.

June 28: Alright, pulled them out of the fridge, soaked them for around three hours, nicked the shells, and put them in soil (Miracle Grow mix with some Flower mix on top and Osmocote pellets mixed in. Turns out there were actually twelve seeds total. Put them in three starter pots (4 each)(6 inch pots, put the seeds 1/2 inch down) and set them inside my greenhouse. Now, the real waiting process begins. They are hot weather, moist soil, humid air thriving plants, so if you grow these, make sure to keep the conditions right, at least until you can put them in soil. I see them in the neighborhood, and there is basically no humidity here, so i assume as long as you keep the soil moist and they get plenty of sun, they will thrive. We shall see though.

July 15th: The first seed sprouted around five days ago. So far, that's all that has happened as of yet.

August 20th: Alright, the one that sprouted was in fact the only seed to sprout. I did follow the instructions provided to a letter,and so i am quite disappointed by the 10% germination rate. The orange "fungus" mentioned in another review might very well have been the problem. I'm left wondering if perhaps, it was actually the seed sprouting due to exposure to heat and/or humidity, thus rendering the steps provided unnecessary and harmful. Dont know for sure. The one plant that is growing is quite healthy, and seems eager to reach its full potential. However, i must change my previous glowing rating to one star. For the $8 you are going to pay overall for this product, the germination rate and questionable seed quality was unacceptable.

Input: I have always been a wood fire BBQ kind of guy - I like meat cooked over a *real* flame, and even charcoal has always seemed to me like cheating (though I've been using charcoal Weber kettle grills for 20 years).  I never even considered a gas grill for myself for these reasons.

For my senior Mom & Dad, however, the task of lighting charcoal, etc was too much hassle, so this past weekend I went out shopping for a gas grill for them.  After going back and forth between three different home centers and Costco, I settled on this unit as by far the best "bang for the buck" in terms of build quality, performance characteristics, and ease of use for under $500.  I seriously considered going up to the Weber Genesis, but for 50% more, I just couldn't quite justify it. My requirement was good quality for under $500.  At this price point, its all about QPR (quality price ratio)...

After about a one-hour erector set project putting it all together (not difficult, just tedious and time consuming), I fired it up and let heat for about 10-15 minutes to get the manufacturing residue completely burned off.  I was immediately impressed with how hot the cooking surfaces became (and how quickly).  The nifty temp sensors at the grate level registered 700+ degrees, though I don't know how accurate they really are.

After burn-off, I tried it out with what I have found to be one of the trickiest things to grill over open flame (gas or wood/charcoal): raw marinated bone-in chicken parts.  To be done right, the chicken has to be crispy on the outside - not burned, and moist and completely cooked on the inside.  With unevenly shaped and sized chicken parts, this can be devilishly tricky.

But with this grill, I found I was able to keep the left most burner at full throttle, and the two right burners at low settings and get creative.  This allowed me to beautifully sear the skin using the left side of the grill, then finish cooking on the right side (with the BBQ closed).  The results were impressive for a gas grill, which in my experience usually turn out either damp, gray, limp chicken with no BBQ taste, or something resembling the effects of a structure fire (charred and dried out) .

One of my favorite things about this grill turned out to be that it is really easy to add wood chips for smoke flavor.  Because there is a perforated metal "screen" (the infrared reflector) under the food, it catches the wood chips and holds them at a perfect smoking temperature where they will smolder but not burn up.

Speaking of flare-ups, this grill did NOT exhibit flare-ups at all.  Even with fatty pieces of chicken that had been marinated in an olive oil mixture, there was almost no burning or excessive smoking, even on the "searing" side of the hot grill.

When turned down low, I also found the evenness of the heating surface to be impressively consistent, and the large stainless "grill" surface not only made great marks on the food, but also did not stick as badly as most coated steel or iron grill surfaces do.

On the con side, I can imagine that the perforated screen is going to require some periodic maintenance to keep it clean.  The good news is that it comes out in three easy-to-handle sections shaped like little trays, each holding a section of grill.  You pull the "tray" up and out, then lift the grill surface out of the tray making both very easy to clean.

One final note - I also prepared a boneless leg of lamb on the grill using a "generic" rotisserie (Grill-Pro brand).  it *barely* fit between the closed lid and the grill surface, but again, the infrared cooking system worked great.  I warmed it up at full throttle for about 5-10 minutes before mounting the marinated lamb roast, then allowed it to sear beautifully for about 15 minutes.  Then I turned the burners all down to their lowest settings, threw on a thumb-sized stick of oak from one of our trees, and dropped the lid.

An hour and a half later, we enjoyed one of the best lamb roasts I have ever had.

Recommended, especially if you can get it for the price I paid (which was about less than Amazon's currently listed price)

Pros:
*Great heat output for searing.  I've not used a gas grill that gets a hotter cooking surface (other than commercial equipment)
*Even distribution of heat for predictable results, very little flare-up.
*Good low-temp performance
*Easy to use wood chips for flavor, unlike many gas grills
*Good (for its price-point) build quality in the hood and firebox.  Cabinets are thin stainless steel.

Cons:
*Bottom 1/2 of construction is a bit flimsy, but better than many at this price point
*Requires pre-heating for about 10 minutes for best results
*Periodic clean-up will be required for optimum performance, and cleanup will be messy

----------
September 2014 update

I can't believe it has been over 5 years since I originally wrote this review.  Interestingly, it has gotten more attention that a lot of my other reviews, so I'll felt I should write a quick update.  I'm visiting my folks and used it three times in the last 4 days.  It has been outside, but covered by a good quality "Brinkmann" cover.  It still performs great and works as well as it did on Day 1.  One thing I've noticed is that it is very sensitive to getting low on fuel.  When the propane tank gets down to about 1/4 full, I swap out to a fresh tank - otherwise it just doesn't get as hot (and I like grilling steaks on a HOT grill).

Great for grilling steaks, chicken, and fish.  Not so great for rotisserie.  if you want to be able to put stuff on a rotisserie, I'd recommend looking elsewhere (the lid fits too close and rubs against the meat).  But for grilling cuts of meat, chicken, or fish, this is a really great piece of gear for the money.  Even fillets of relatively soft fish like trout and salmon don't stick to the grill, and fatty pieces of steak or chicken don't flare up and burn.  I continue to be impressed.

When someone figures out how to let the operator unwind the string manually from a trigger/release without stopping they will dominate this market.
I took a star off my rating because of the automatic string advance, and overall I still like and use the unit because on every other aspect it met or exceeded my expectations.

Input: Over the last 8 years I've gone through 2 of the smaller Farmhouse model, and have been very pleased with the how they protected my tropical plants from the occasional freezes we get in South Louisiana.  This year I needed more space so I decided to get the larger Farmhouse XL version.  I figured it would be more difficult it would be to assemble, but I had put together the smaller version by myself so I figured I would be able to manage this one too.

Well I was wrong.  Believe me and the instruction that come with the XL version: you will need 3 people to put this thing up!!! (Or two people and two sturdy trees.)

Assembly of the greenhouse is pretty straightforward if you follow the instruction to the letter, and keep telling yourself that all the pieces WILL eventually fit together.  You also need a lot of brute strength, sweat, and some cursing.  The fit is unbelievable tight, and after assembling the first few poles you think, "no way will this thing fit together, they sent me the wrong poles."  But in the end all the pieces do fit, and you will get the greenhouse in the picture.

Observations:

&#10003 The greenhouse is easy to assemble if you have 3 people and a lot of brute strength to push, pull and force the poles into position.

&#10003 You will need a heater to keep the greenhouse warm on cold days/nights.  Without a heater the interior of the greenhouse is the same temperature as the air outside.

&#10003 On a sunny day the temperature inside the greenhouse will skyrocket.  You need to monitor the temperature and open the windows and the doors as needed.

&#10003 It gets very humid inside the greenhouse.  You need a heater that can take all the moisture or move the heater in and out every day.

&#10003 The greenhouse will only last 3-4 seasons.  The fiberglass frame creates a lot of pressure against the plastic shell, and after a few years the plastic around the pressure points starts to fray.  The greenhouse also gets very dirty from dead leaves and bugs that accumulate around the bottom edge.

&#10003 Even though the product description says the XL has 2 screen doors and 12 screen windows there is NO screening.  Honestly I never used the door screens on my smaller Farmhouse so the lack of screens does not bother me.  The greenhouse is in my fenced back yard so I don't have a problem with animals getting in.  Although I do get lots of flying bugs, frogs, and once a small grass snake.

&#10003 The product description also said that the XL can zip to another greenhouse, but this is not accurate either.  The regular size Farmhouse had the zipper which allowed you to chain multiple greenhouses together, but the XL does not.

&#10003 This is a minor issue, but I not like the green cords that are used for high wind tie downs.  The green color makes them hard to see.  I've run into them many times while taking the dog outside in the middle of the night.  I now use neon orange cord as my tie downs.

&#10003 Disassembling the green house is a snap. One person can take it down in a matter of minutes.  But good luck getting the greenhouse back into its storage bag.  Folding it small enough takes a lot of brute force and "Twister" like moves.

 So all-in-all I'm very pleased with my XL Farmhouse.  It is a pain to assemble, but 45 minutes of aggravation is worth it to save all my delicate plants.

Input: Last winter the deer ate almost everything in the yard, even though most were surrounded by 4' fencing that had deterred them in the past. The deer just pushed them down and stood on the crumpled remains to get to higher branches. Even the supposedly deer-resistant holly bushes got eaten. Lo, these many months later, they still look ragged. This winter, we're trying out this netting.

It went on with little trouble, it just took the first bush to figure out how best to handle it - one roll wrapped two holly and two rhododendron. From a distance, I can't tell they're wrapped at all - the mesh is so fine, and the black color helps to hide it as well. The netting is doubled over on the roll so after unrolling you have to unfold it to its full height. I found the best way to do this is to first find the side where the fold is and keep that on top. Put the roll against the bush, positioning it so the roll is on the outside. Affix the end of the back side to the bush with zip ties, attaching at the top by the fold and at the bottom. This keeps the netting from moving while unrolling. Unroll the netting, walking around the bush and keeping the netting snug until the starting point is reached. This stuff stretches, so overlap wasn't really needed. Cut with scissors. Secure the bottom of the cut end with zip ties. Now find the free bottom edge and lift the netting to full height, placing it on the shrub at the desired height. Secure top and bottom edges with zip ties in several spots around the bush.

The netting sticks to every twig and branch, so not many zip ties are needed, especially at the top - just enough to keep it from blowing or falling as wind moves the tree. More zips were needed at the bottom, as this is where the deer will try to push under it. In the spring it'll likely be difficult to remove intact - it catches on everything - so I'm anticipating this to be a single-use product. I'll report back in the spring and give it five starts if it keeps the deer from eating the landscaping.

Update 3/27/17: It worked great in year 1 but year 2 saw a heavy snowfall and pack of ravenous deer combine to overwhelm it. The weight of 2' of snow pushed holly and rhododendron branches toward the ground. Some of the netting tore from the stress. The deer, standing in the deep snow and on top of the lower branches, could reach the unprotected upper branches while their weight pulled the netting lower and tore it further.

Input: I have 7 of these around the perimeter of my yard and they have worked fine for the past 2 years.  I bought these (one or two at a time) because I have very hard well water and normal impact sprinklers would clog up with calcium deposits.  I haven't had any problems with these Orbit gear-drive sprinklers.

There are 3 controls for the units.  The green disk on top sets the spray effect (short, medium, or long) buy inserting a tooth into the water stream.  So if you want a long distance, the tooth is minimal.  If you want a short distance then the tooth is large.  I just rotate the top green disk to set this.

The second control is the next ring down that controls the spray pattern: stream, mist, etc.  There are about 8 options (sorry, I didn't walk outside to count them).

The last control are the two green rings at the bottom and these control the start and stop sweep angle.  So I can go all the way around (360 degrees), or limit it to a smaller angle.  Note however, that even if you a line the start and stop, it goes all the way around one way, then back all the way around the other.  That's just the way the gear-drive Orbit unit works.  It won't keep spinning around and around the same way like a free spinning impact sprinkler (with the reversing stops removed).  It isn't a problem, just be aware of it ahead of time.

I gave this only 4 stars because there are 2 things that this design lacks:  (1) a hose screw ring and (2) a range limiter.  (1) In order to screw this onto a garden hose, you have to spin the entire silver colored body onto the hose.  Not a big deal since I use this in a semi-permanent installation.  (2) A range limiter would allow me to set some small portion that limits the range (instead of limiting the range for the whole circle).  I'd like to use the "long" range to form a large circle, but also have some range limiter to prevent the spray from hitting the house (and calcifying the wall and wooden fence).  Other people make stand-alone metal posts that do this, I'd just like it to be included in the sprinkler.

Anyway, I've been very happy with my seven 2-year old units.

Scott Nelson

Input: Here is what I like:

Fairly lightweight

Sharp

Nice holder/protector

Handle shape shouldn't allow flying out of hand

What I found a bit unlikeable:

Sharp edge is a bit fragile. After using for a few hours the edge was a bit beat-up-looking. And no, I did not strike anything but the end of the log I was splitting.

The axe will get stuck. It comes out fairly easily most of the time but several times I had to work to get the blade free.

The axe bounced off some of the wood I was attempting to split - would not penetrate. Bouncing off was nowhere near as bad as it was with my 8 pound splitter, but was still more of a problem than I expected from reading the reviews. On the other hand I also have a Gransfors-Bruks small splitting axe and it does NOT bounce off.

Some logs I worked on (all cut to 16" long and from 6" to 16" diameter hardwoods - oak, maple, some kind of nut) required multiple hits to start a split. I beat a few into submission with this axe and was disappointed that it took so many hits to finish splitting. I found the easiest way to do the job was to use this axe to make starter splits (one or two hits on each spot I wanted a split) then finish it with the 8 pounder.

Bottom line is this axe is very good for some logs, especially straight-grained oak, which split cleanly with one hit. It is not as good if the wood is hard enough and dense enough to cause the axe to bounce off. You will also NOT want to leave your heavy splitting maul in the garage - it will still be the best tool for some wood. I haven't touched up the edge of this axe yet to remove the ragged edge from a few hundred hits on log ends but when I do I think I will try making the edge angle a bit less acute to give it a bit more strength. As is the case with every hand-splitting tool the wood is the determining factor. No one tool works for everything.

I have a LOT of experience splitting firewood by hand. I've been splitting my own wood since 1978 (with a few years break when I didn't have a stove) and have tried lots of different tools. Most have been commercial axes and various wedges plus a few I've made myself. In the end nothing beats wedges and a sledge hammer when a splitting axe just doesn't do the job.

Input: The manufacturer claims that the Dynatrap produces carbon dioxide (CO2) through an exclusive titanium dioxide (TiO2) surface.  Indeed TiO2 surfaces will catalyze the production of CO2 when a suitable hydrocarbon is present.  I am a chemist and know about these things.  Since the Dynatrap does not use propane, what is the source of hydrocarbon?  Insect bodies?  Small amounts of hydrocarbons in the air?  Because the claim did not make sense to me, I decided to use a CO2 meter (a CO2Meter model AZ0004) to  determine whether CO2 is actually produced by the Dynatrap. I placed the meter just below the basket where the insects are trapped due to the downward flow air from the fan.  The CO2 meter read 396 ppm, which is the same as outdoor air in my area.  I placed the meter at several spots  around the Dynatrap and detected NO CO2 above the ambient level of 396 ppm normally found in air.  In other words, the Dynatrap did not produce any measurable CO2.  By comparison, one breath from me toward the meter caused it to spike its reading from 396 ppm to 1944 ppm - a five fold increase!  I then measured the CO2 output from a Megacatch Ultra mosquito trap that runs on a CO2 cylinder.  The Megacatch releases CO2 in puffs.  At a modest CO2 release setting of 2 (the Megacatch has release settings between 1 and 5), the CO2 meter reading would spike to about 950 ppm with each puff - about 2.5-fold increase over the ambient level in air.  Since CO2 is the major attractant for mosquitos, the test with the Dynatrap was disappointing.  However, its black color, water tray and UV light serve as insect attractants despite no CO2 being produced by the Dynatrap  After running the Dynatrap 24/7 for a week, the basket was filled mostly with moths but there were some mosquitos as well.  The Megacatch had trapped about five times more mosquitos than the Dynatrap.  The water tray of the Dynatrap had some drowned beetles and moths.  I give the Dynatrap a 3 star rating because it does catch some mosquitos and it is not terribly expensive as mosquito traps go.  It is much less expensive than Mosquito Magnets and Megacatchs.  The Dynatrap would likely trap many more mosquitos if it actually produced CO2.

Input: The product arrived damaged. A piece had been broken out of the orange blade housing near the right rear wheel. The plastic mount on the right side where the handle attached to the deck was also cracked. This mower appears to have been returned and the resold. The shipping box was not the original - two plain cardboard boxes had been taped together to create one large box for the mower. Part of the original Black & Decker box had been used inside to create some internal box packing. Interestingly, included in the shipping container was 3/4 of a pint plastic bottle of 4 cycle lawnmower oil!

The mower is considered hazardous material, soit could not be returned. Amazon was very prompt about refunding the purchase price.

In spite of the shipping damage, the mower was sufficiently functional to test out before it totally breaks down.

I have 4000-5000 sq ft of St. Augustine grass. The lawn was fairly high since my old mower broke down a few weeks ago, but not particularly thick due to shade. After an initial overnight charge, the mower handled the hour of work without any apparent loss of power. The high grass was not a problem either - the motor slowed a bit where the grass was thickest, but did not bog down.

The single lever height adjustment is really a nice feature, working very smoothly and easily. The light weight, low noise level, and instant start are welcome changes from the old gas machine.

The battery does not have any power indicator - a desirable feature that is missing.

The mower seems somewhat flimsy (note shipping damage above). You feel the need to be extra careful when maneuvering around trees, fences and landscape timbers so as not to damage a wheel or crack something. The wheels are fairly small and narrow, allowing the mover to sink into any turf that is soft or spongy. Was not a big problem on my test mow, but when I have to use the bag during leaf season (that is spring for us in Florida), the extra weight will make it more noticeable. Wider wheels would distribute the weight better and roll easier.

Input: Been using my Weedeater One now for about 3 years - I've found it to be a fairly well designed minimalist riding mower, but with increasing negatives. The round plastic gear at the top of the steering column under the steering wheel did round off the first mowing season, but the replacement part is metal & won't round off. More horsepower would be nice, but I've had no real problems climbing shallow gradients; if you have steep hills, you need a more powerful mower.

I added the bagger kit during the 2nd mowing season (ordered through Amazon); directions are simple & accurate & I had no problem installing it. Except for the small bags, the bagger works ok. Note: the rubber seal that fits around the edge of the bagger cover hole is purposely not round (neither is the hole) - just rotate it to fit the hole when installing and it should stay in place when lifting the cover to empty the bags. Also, be sure to use the replacement blade in the kit - it creates more suction and gets the grass/leaves up into the bags better than the original blade.

Finally, to the point of this review: the small original bags only have a total capacity of 3 bushels & thus must be emptied often. After some research online, I found the exact same design bags available from Sears with double the capacity (6 bushels). The longer bags have Sears part number 400226, description is "bag soft" or "container"; cost is $46.71 per bag (plus shipping) and can be ordered from Sears Parts Direct at 1-800-252-1698. The online price is higher ($52.50), so save some money & order by phone. The replacement bags are pricey, but they transform the Weedeater One bagger into a truly usable tool for sucking up those grass clippings & leaves.

Input: The box had arrived damage where the spool head was sticking out. But no damage to it that I can see. I had to wait for a couple of days due to heavy rain storms here. Yesterday was the very first time using this unit. As it's the 4th 40v 4amp Greenworks garden tool I've purchased on Amazon this year. I had purchased RYOBI from Home Depot their version of the 40v cordless lithium ion string trimmer and edger. Well that one and this one seems to share a lot. Like they don't advance the line when they should and suffer from the glitch that causes it. Greenworks model is better, it allows you to get a deep trench edging right deep into the dirt. Keeping that steady is a challenge! But the line feed is the major selling point here. These units are suppose to automatically advance the line for you. I need such a feature. But after getting 3/4 of the line stool down, sure enough I could see that the line never advanced out. Just like the RYOBI model from Home Depot did on me. I had said oh no not again!

Not even tightly rounded like it should be. Strange how both models are doing the same thing. These are made by Homelite then since that's how makes the RYOBI but Greenwise has multi-head adjustments instead of the 90' degree turning head it has flex pole angles giving you all sorts of ranges to trim and edge. I find that a very neat feature to have. My edge of my lawn looks better than it did using the RYOBI RY40210 93WH where has the Greenworks model this one has 146WH and it's more powerful than the RYOBI one. The only other difference is the line advancement one has 13" on RY40210 and the Greenworks has 12". But you only get 6" on both models. When you buy the units you get the full length but something odd happens when you use it. I guess the one reviewer was right it cuts the line in half.

Also the spool of line when it gets to 1/2 or 3/4 it won't spool out any more. I have to stop it and then do a manually feed of line through the hole then it continues on. Best not even bother with that line notch to hold the line as either that feature is defective or it just doesn't cut the water. I had order that 3x pack of line spool here off Amazon just in case. So now I know this model going to end up being replaced or exchanged. There just not enough choices in this market for such a unit and not at the full battery DC 146WH. You don't want the 93WH not going to last too long an power dies too fast on the RYOBI model.

I've given this just 3 stars because the button layout is poor on the Greenworks model. My fingers hurt after pushing and pressing the control buttons. They could have made it better. Then it's top heavy with the fat battery on top. Same design as the RYOBI 40v but that one is more balanced and ligher. But RYOBI the wheel use on the edger is weakest feature it wears out too fast. The one on the Greenworks is more heavy duty and can be easy to change out in parts. They need to tighten the knot at the factory. I had to do it. The controls on both models are the weakest areas too. RYOBI it could break off as you got to grabs to long rods as with the Greenworks you and push and grab. The push part hurts your finger after a long time.

Greenworks did a better job with how the unit flexes and center loop holder has better flex feature as well. I did see a hole on the top to hang the unit on the wall. There is also a strap clip holder but that feature didn't come with this model. Same with the RYOBI.

Sending this one back to Amazon to get one that does have Auto Advancement in Line going to be interesting to see what I get back? One more defect I've notice was the battery charger unit when you push in the battery it still shows red and green on a dead battery. That's because you have to use a rubber mallet to tap the battery into the charger for it to work right. I did see that the one pin was bent. Un-bending it didn't seem to do the trick. That means it off alignment.

I best get this ready to go back to them tomorrow... 6.1.12 for a replacement!

I'll keep you updated on my progress..

6.7.12
Replacement had arrived. This one was much better. Less than 10 minutes I had assemble it. I did the flip around for the cutter put so the length will be longer than shorter. If you find yours defective just let Amazon know and they'll take good care of you. The battery charger was easy to use this time slide and lock. Not slide and bend like prior one did!

**6.14.12***
This is just keeping worst and worst. I see others are complaining about the weight yep I have too join club on that one. But biggest issue right now is that the auto-line head is not working as advertise. It won't advance! I have to stop open the cover and feed in the line. Now the 90 degree head won't lock into place either. No I didn't use my foot. I had stopped and did this manual with my hand. Both adjustments are not working like the spring or hinge inside is broken. This is a shame it has full power off the bat. But Edging is awful. Not balance and no auto-line feed. To me when I first got the second replacement it work with a full line as the line gets down then there is issues. I had even ordered replacement lines. This one going back and I'll looking at Toro 24V for a replacement off Amazon.

Pros
Power of 40V 4amp 146WH

Cons
Edging doesn't mean auto-line feed
Line is only less than 6-inches never 10-13 inches as the box reads the the label on the unit
Battery seems to drain much more on the model
90 degree adjustment head can stick or not lock into position
Adjustable head from the pole can also not lock into angle positions
Weight Balance is off
Hold the trigger button and the other grabber button for advancements doesn't always work out right
Quality on this one is not up to par

Input: These are great little boxes for organizing my bathroom vanity. Perfect size and seem quite sturdy.

That being said, they still use the horribly sticky labels that many reviewers have mentioned. It's not a deal-breaker for me, but it will be time consuming to remove. I forgot about the reviews I had read, and when they arrived I quickly pulled off the labels on the first box. Big mistake, as you can see in the photos. They use several extremely adhesive circles per label. My hubby threw it into hot soapy water and was able to scrub it off cleanly in about 5 minutes.

 I wouldn't use Goo Gone or any acetone product as I think it would cloud the plastic, as other reviewers have mentioned.  UPDATE: I tried a 1:1 mix of vegetable oil and baking soda to remove a particularly sticky spot. It worked like a charm, but the abrasive nature of the baking soda did in fact scratch the plastic and left it a bit cloudy. See photos- clouded side vs unclouded side. Still better than the sticky spot!

Anyway as I said, not a deal-breaker for me.  Yes I paid money for them, and I still feel it was a fair price despite the extra work. I mean honestly, I clicked a magic button on my phone and these arrived on my doorstep two days later. That's pretty amazing. I don't want to lose sight of that!  Yay Amazon!

Input: Purchased along with the Harp Earring rack so my bracelets & necklaces could be organized. The earring section works great for studs & some shorter hook style earrings, but the distance between each rack is only 2 & 1/4" long so dangle earrings hang over the next row making it a little clumsy when selecting earrings. Reason 1 for the lower rating.

I was quite disappointed when I hung the first necklace on the hook provided and it touched the shelf the organizer was sitting on. I tried two others & the same thing happened, so I measured the length where the bend is in the hook to the base of the organizer & it was only 9" long. Since all my necklaces, except one, average 10" in length, none of them could be hung on this side of the organizer, so it is now being used as a bracelet organizer which does work efficiently. Reason 2 for the lower rating.

I do have some heavy linked bracelets that do not work with the hooks since they don't hang loosely, not to mention there isn't a lot of distance between the hooks themselves. The hooks are more suited for 'fine' jewelry pieces versus chunky styles. So those bracelets have been hooked over the rungs for earrings & do display the beauty of the bracelets in grand style & they are easy to remove at a moments notice with no effort at all.

I used the curved pieces at the top of the organizer for a couple of stretch style chunky bracelets & that worked well.

The organizer can also be used for any type of lapel pin, tie tack & watch. It's sturdy, well made & worth the price paid.

I do recommend as long as you don't have a lot of chunky, clunky jewelry. If you do, you might want to look for a different style organizer.

They suggest setting the Pillow on one end on a chair when filling and that made it very simple both to fill and to press out the air bubbles.  Then just tighten the valve, and you're all set.  There is a thick soft layer of padding above the water bladder, so it never feels cold.  I find that it's very comfortable and cradles my head perfectly.  My husband likes his too.

There is a product code included with each pillow where you can "like" them on Facebook and get a free hypoallergenic pillow cover. Input: Sadly, this canister is about as lightweight and flimsy as any flip-top style container I have handled. Too bad because it looks nice in the pictures and even from a few feet away, but once you handle it the challenges are quickly exposed.

That said - it is correctly described in the listing as weighing just 9.4 ounces... the paperback book in my hand right now weighs 30% more at 12.2 ounces. Six inches tall, five inches in diameter, a top, gasket and closing mechanism... combining for just 9.4 ounces.

Summarizing as briefly as possible: The metal of the canister is very thin; The lid of the canister is made of plastic and the injection molding tabs have not even been polished off (hard and rough little stubs around the edge); The rubber gasket needed for the airtight seal is poorly fitted under the lid and falls out each time the lid is opened; The gasket is next to impossible to get back into the lid's groove so that the closing mechanism has a chance of sealing properly; The closing mechanism does not apply enough pressure to push the plastic lid all the way down over the gasket and create a good seal; The wire ring part of the lid closing mechanism is so flimsy that we have a difficult time lining the lid up with the canister when trying to lock the lid closed. More often than not we give up and just close it off-center (therefore not airtight).

I did receive this unit gratis from the manufacturer and we tried to put it through its paces to objectively find out how well it performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

Am thinking about taking it into work and just putting it in the break area filled with things that do not need an airtight seal like M&Ms, gum balls, or jelly beans. Still, at the current price that's not worth a second star.

This review is from a petite females perspective
I was browsing for couple months and this Serta chair stood out to me, mainly aesthetically. I don't see many chairs in this color or style. It matched with the rest of my PC/desk setup.

Positives
-Seat is comfortable.
-My back feels nicely supported. It helps me sit very straight.
-The casters were surprisingly easy to put in. I had to use some force with two of them though. They roll fine on carpet.
-Easy assembly

Neutral/Negatives
-Paint of armrests is easily scratched. I accidentally scratched it while installing the back.
-The black plastic caps used to hide the screws don't fit well. The plastic inserts for hiding screws in arms don't fit well either. It makes the chair appear cheap. (I will provide images)

-Craftsmanship isn't the best.
-At lowest setting, my feet cant touch the ground but being 411 its to be expected.
-Seat back height is a little high for my liking/comfort.  I prefer couple inches shorter so I can sometimes rest my head back rather than getting blocked by the seat.
-Head area (or shoulder rest to some) is too firm. I prefer it to be squishy.
-Adjustable arm positioning? No, thats a false advertisement.
-Customization? There is barely any besides height. The left lever I believe supposed to adjust the chair tilt but maybe Im too light to notice any difference.

As another reviewer mentioned, don't forget to remove the foam or cardboard behind the lumbar and head/shoulder. That is supposedly the last step when assembly is all done.

**If you come across any issues/warranty, you contact TRUE INNOVATIONS, not Serta. (I will provide images)

Input: I ordered this unit as I have been looking for a white corner cabinet for my stereo system.  This model, the Homes Styles Bermuda Corner TV stand looked just right, as it matched the decor of the room.  Some of the reviewers here on amazon.com have commented that it takes too long to assemble.  Unpacking and assembly plus the additional work that I had to do took about 3 hours.  I have put together similar cabinets before and I was expecting it to take some time to complete it, so I allocated my time accordingly.  Cabinets like this don't just "pop" into place with the push of a button.  These things do take time and when you are working with MDF material you have to be careful as it can very easily chip.  There are many angles and corners so you have to make sure that each piece is straight and level before moving to the next step.  Don't tighten everything until the last step and make sure everything is square.  It really helps if you have someone to hold each section as you tighten the screws.  That being said, the assembly instructions are rather poor.  They consist of simple drawings, not pictures, without much of a written description as to how to proceed.

As others have commented, the cabinet pieces were packed very poorly and I agree.  Everything is crammed into one cardboard box with pieces of styrofoam for padding and tyvek like cloth to prevent scratches.  The cardboard box was rather thin considering the weight of the MDF pieces.  This should have been more securely packed using two boxes rather than one.  Three pieces were chipped; luckily the chips are on the back where they won't be seen! I had to redrill the hole for one door hinge as the predrilled holes were too high, not allowing the door to close without rubbing against the top. Also, the mounting point for the door magnet was broken so I had to glue it and wait for the glue to set overnight before I screwed on the hardware. Minus one star for poor packing.

In addition, I drilled two smaller holes in the back to allow for more cables and speaker wires to snake though (I am connecting to a surround sound receiver and using several analog cables).  I drilled holes on each side of the shelf to allow for better air flow as my receiver just fits in the space.  My receiver can tend to get hot if it is played loud for long periods of time.  I have a small box fan that I can use for those rare occasions.

I am a firm believer in the old adage "you get what you pay for". The amazon price was a good value compared to some other internet prices.  I knew from the moment I ordered it that this was not going to be fine furniture, but it does look really nice and it is being utilized as I intended with just a few modifications.

Input: We had one of these when I was a kid. I was recently looking for a better and healthier way to pop popcorn (other than the unhealthy microwave bags, or the unreliable microwave poppers or the air poppers that create tasteless popcorn) and was pleased to find that this is still being made. Upon receiving it, I was disappointed to find that the bowl/cover was much flimsier than the old ones. Also the plastic cover over the butter receptacle did not hold as tightly as one might like. And I was disappointed that the stir rod was bent incorrectly at the factory, allowing one side of it to scrape quite severely on the cooking surface; if left like that the nonstick coating would have scraped off in no time. Luckily, it is made to come off and after fiddling with it for about 15-20 minutes, I was able to get it bent correctly so it just barely clears the cooking surface.

Having said that, it pops great. My first batch did not have a single unpopped kernel! Not all batches come out that great, but it has the best performance I have ever seen in a popper. And I have found some new ways to use my Stir Crazy:

If you want that true movie theater taste (though not terribly healthy), I would recommend the "Real Movie Theater" premeasured pouches from Wabash Valley Farms, especially the less oil, less salt version which actually tastes better and is not greasy like the regular version. Just snip open the pouch, and toss in the premeasured oil, corn and salt/seasoning and let 'er pop--you will get evenly salted and seasoned popcorn that tastes as good as any theater popcorn.

And believe it or not, you can make caramel popcorn (or even candy-coated popcorn) by using "Glaze-Pop"--this is what the theaters use. In three minutes you will have delicious caramel or candy-coated popcorn, I promise! You can find it for $4 a box or less on the web if you shop around. I am including instructions for use here, as the box only has instructions for commercial poppers: put in two tablespoons of oil, then add 2/3 cup of the Glaze Pop flavoring of your choice, then add 1/3 cup of (unpopped) popcorn. Let it pop just as if you were popping regular corn (do not add salt). If you want to pop more corn, adjust ingredient quantities upward accordingly. Cleanup is easy, just carefully wipe off the popper surface with a wad of paper towels before it cools; flavoring easily washes off the domed lid. Coverage will not be as even as if you spent an hour slaving over the stove making the caramel and stirring it into the popcorn, but every kernel will get enough flavoring so there no mistaking that you are eating caramel (or whatever flavor you chose) popcorn. My favorite flavors are the caramel, the chocolate (popcorn tastes like chocolate cereal) and the cinnamon. A note of caution, the food coloring used for red and especially the purple and blue flavors can easily stain whatever they come into contact with, even your fingers!

Input: I don't normally write reviews about inexpensive housewares, but I fixed an issue with my unit that I think might help others with the same issue.  When the unit arrived, I was unable to get the alarm to work and the LED light wouldn't illuminate.  The unit ships with two cheap, off-brand AAA batteries already installed.  Most manufacturers will either keep the batteries separate or they'll place a thin piece of plastic between the battery terminals and the contacts to keep them from draining before sale, but not this company. I thought that perhaps the reason was that the unit was designed to reduce battery drain when the batteries are low by disabling those features and, by golly, I was right.  After installing a brand new set of Costco AAA batteries the alarm and LED worked fine.

So before you attempt a return on the product, change the batteries even if the unit is brand-new.

Input: I 've had Rosacea on since my teenage years and spent 40+ years putting up with recurring outbreaks attributing it to stress. Well it is stress related but about 10 years ago during a routine appointment my Dr. took notice and identified it. There was a name for this? Who knew? She prescribed Metro gel which had a small effect but I found it ridiculously drying and sometimes irritating to my skin so I only used it if I had a bad outbreak. I found Prosacea  about 5 years ago at a Walgreens when shopping for something else. Intrigued I checked the ingredients. Sulpher. Then I remembered that sulpher is used in homeopathic medications as well as special soaps for acne. Bought it, tried it and it worked. Dramatically. Like "RIGHT NOW". I saw redness fade within 20 minutes at the notorious cheek to nose creases. You know the ones. The inflamed, tender, crusty, oily, complete strangers staring at you, the gentle inquiry of "What's wrong with your face?"
Prosacea says enough of that. Even the worst oubreak is clear in 24 hours. It works for me. I don't even have to use it every day for it to be effective. Problem solved? Not exactly. Rosacea is actually a very complex condition with many possible contributing factors. Stress, hygiene, diet, heat, strenuous activity, and alcohol can factor in. There is also solid research that microbial activity from fauna normally found on our skin can be a cause. There isn't a cure for Rosacea, by the way, it's a condition that can be managed quite well. Because it is affected by many different things it doesn't surprise me that some people respond well to Prosacea while some might not. Input: We have been using various "natural" peanut butters for years, switching as soon as we learned about the dangers of partially hydrogenated oils. "Natural" is the industry code word for no hydrogenated oils, and we always look for it because even "reduced fat" peanut butters have hydrogenated oils if they're not labeled "natural."  We've tried so many brands over the years, including Skippy which tends to have slightly more saturated fat than other natural blends.

As a family we tend to prefer the more boutique brand, Peanut Butter & Co. Among the basic go-to brands, we agree that Jif Natural has a more robust roasted peanut taste. This Skippy seems a little bland by comparison, although it has that same classic Skippy taste, meaning we detected no real difference taste-wise between this natural version and the regular (hydrogenated oils) version. Per a two tablespoon serving, Skippy Natural has 3.5 grams of saturated fat (other brands have 2.5 or 3 roughly), and 3 grams of sugar. We found that the Skippy Natural with Honey (5 grams of sugar) tastes better all around.

Skippy Natural may never be our absolute favorite peanut butter brand, though it does offer a recognizably pleasing peanut taste, no hydrogenated oils, and a good value compared to more boutique natural brands. If your family is thinking about going "natural," at least with peanut butter, Skippy is worth a shot.

Input: I have used Strivectin three times a day for about three years. Being 45, I would have appreciated the disappearance of some lines or wrinkles.  However, there is absolutely no change in them with Strivectin. I find the claims to be bogus and I'm glad the FDA has been investigating them.

On the other hand, this moisturizer feels better on my skin than any other I've used. I love the feeling of it! Peppermint is what makes it feel cool but apart from that it is wonderfully thick and luscious on the skin without being sticky or oily.  Of course, there are probably moisturizers for a quarter of the cost that feel just as good. The problem is that most moisturizers are for women and contain scents that are supposed to appeal to women (although I cannot imagine how they would). Strivectin does not contain strong scent so it is suitable for men to wear.

Therefore I give this 0/5 stars for doing what it says it does - because the claims made for the product are bogus based on my experience. I give this product 2/5 for being a good men's moisturizer but it is way too expensive for a mere moisturizer so cannot be rated more highly than 2/5.

Feel free to ignore the tedious and specific content. Just focus on some general textual attributes! Input: The main problem with this product is that it is overpriced and completely unnecessary. Lip exfoliation is one of the simplest, most inexpensive beauty routines one can engage in at home because it only requires two basic ingredients that virtually every household has on hand: sugar and oil. Specifically, all that is required to exfoliate the lips is a tiny amount of granular sugar, either white table sugar (sucrose as in this product), brown sugar, raw sugar, or sugar alcohol such as xylitol. Add to that an equal amount of any food-grade oil you have on hand in the house, for example: olive oil, canola oil, safflower oil, or coconut oil. One-fourth teaspoon each of granular sugar and oil is enough to do both lips. The instructions for do-it-yourself exfoliation are as follows: In a small bowl or saucer, measure out one-fourth teaspoon of granular sugar. On top of it put an equal amount of oil. Wash your hands and dry them thoroughly. Blend the sugar and oil together with the tip of your finger. Rub the sugar-oil mixture onto your lips in a circular motion for two-five minutes. Gently scrub off the mixture with a clean, damp washcloth to remove not only the sugar and oil, but any loosened, dead skin. If flaking, dead skin still remains on your lips, rub more of the sugar-oil mixture onto your lips and repeat the above process. After you are finished, immediately moisturize your lips, ideally with a natural, food-grade oil or a lip balm made with an oil-beeswax mixture, since anything that goes on the lips ultimately ends up in the mouth and stomach. The second problem with this product is that even though the container looks small, there is enough of this product to last a very long time. And while it is sitting on your bathroom shelf, it is slowly drying out. Within six months to a year, long before you've used more than a fraction of it, this product will deteriorate into a hard, unusable lump (not to mention that most cosmetics companies recommend throwing out their products anyway within six to nine months because of inevitable bacteria buildup). If you make your own sugar-oil mixture each time you need it, nothing is wasted, and it is always fresh, with a smooth, viscous consistency that glides onto your lips. The third problem with this product is that, though some of the ingredients are natural and food-grade, others are not. The ingredients for this product include: "Sucrose, Petrolatum, Flavor, Caramel, Simmondsia Chinensis (Jojoba) Seed Oil, VitiVinifera (Grape) Seed Oil." Below is a description of each ingredient. The most problematic one is petrolatum. It is too bad that the makers of this product didn't just stick to grapeseed oil, which is a natural, healthy oil. Sucrose is simple white/table sugar. Petrolatum: This lab-derived substance has been around since 1859 when chemist Robert Chesebrough developed a method of purifying a black gel that clogged oil rigs called "rod wax." This is a very thick substance which is anything but ideal for exfoliating the skin. Flavor: It is not specified whether this is "artificial" or "natural" flavor. Artificial flavor is derived from non-food substances, that is, chemicals created in a lab. Natural flavor is derived from a real food, but the process by which it is derived is unexplained. In both cases, there is no way to know how safe or healthy the flavoring is. Caramel: This is sugar or syrup heated until it turns brown. It can either be used as a coloring agent or to impart flavor. Jojoba oil is a natural plant oil. It is created from the liquid wax of the seed of the jojoba plant, a shrub which is native to southern Arizona, southern California, and northwestern Mexico. It's much healthier than petrolatum, but it contains 14% erucic acid, which is not recommended to be taken internally. Grapeseed oil is a natural oil derived from the seeds of grape. Input: Tried these out today finally. They had a bit of a scent but it wasn't unpleasant at all. The directions said 10 to 15 minutes to leave it on, I settled for 12 for an in-between. I was a bit worried when it didn't get quite as stiff as other pore strips I've used, however, it ended up working really well, if not better, than others I've tried (though, for the record, I haven't tried too many. Mostly Biore). It got rid of more blackheads than the other strips I've used, leaving me shocked in just how many I actually had and didn't know. I would totally order these again in the future because they really do a fantastic job. My nose has a funny little tingle now, but it's a nice feeling, since it makes me feel like it really did a good job cleaning out my pores.
My only minor complaint was that they did leave a white residue behind on the lower parts of my nose by the tip, but nothing that can't be washed off after.

Edit, after buying a second package: I knocked my rating down to four stars. The second package I bought had charcoal added as an ingredient, which in itself wasn't a big deal because I knew it was a popular trend now. However, I don't know if the charcoal affects the strip or not, but I've noticed with these that the outer portion of the strip becomes very sticky when applying it (no matter how much I dry my hands first) and you can see the material sticking to your fingers. It wouldn't be a big deal but it does make me question the effectiveness now, and it does prevent me from sticking it to my nose properly because I don't want to end up pulling all the goo off. I might buy a third box at some point to see if I just got a dud box, but I would not buy a forth if it continues.

And in a downwards angle.  I do this entire routine two to four times a day.  After two days my blackheads were gone.  After a week, my skin looked like porcelain.

I applied this first at night and when I woke up, the circles were more smooth and less dark by about a shade.  By the second day, the skin around my eyes, where the faint crows feet were, the skin looked fuller and you could barely see the lines.  The improvements continued for 3-5 days and have since plateaued at a nice place-firm skin around the eyes and very minimal circles.

I am not sure how long these results will last when I stop using this cream, but it really does work.  The reason I gave it 4/5 stars is the price-it is currently listed at $125 per 0.5 oz. container.  I do like it, however, I just can't see spending that kind of money regularly especially given this is only for the eyes, it's not designed to even be used on the the other parts of your face.

Overall, it works great, and in this case, it should b/c you may have to sell your first born child to purchase it regularly-however, this stuff will make you look so young no one would believe you've had kids anyway, so there you go ;)

I am normally scent-sensitive, so when I was at the spa at a resort and realized the only sunscreen I had was in my makeup, I bought this. First, after sniffing the testers, I bought the unscented version--and within five minutes of putting it on, I smelled like rotting fish dipped in not-quite-dry oil-based house paint. I showered, went back to the spa and they let me exchange it for the Fresh Mango scented version--which tester smelled delightful. Put it on today, and I smelled great.....for maybe half an hour (the instructions say to wait 20 minutes after applying it to go out in the sun. Then the mango scent was gone, replaced by that fishy-painty stench. Every place I went to shop, I had to duck into the restroom to wash my hands, forearms and cleavage. Within five minutes, the stink had come back. It ruined my appetite at the coffee and fro-yo bars, and Im sure other people noticed it too--so embarrassing! (Hoping the beans I ate do their job--even flatulence smells better). I looked at the ingredient list, and voil: LINSEED OIL. Yup, the very stuff they use to make oil and house paints. And Lancomes constant reminder that this ingredient is protected by 20 patents makes it seem even more remarkablebut a patent has nothing to do with efficacy; it is only about a unique way to use any ingredient. A patent can be obtained simply by presenting an idea, not proof that the idea actually works.

As it turns out, simply propelling an ingredient through skin is not a guarantee of anything beneficial happening, and it may even make matters worse. For example, many ingredients, such as sunscreen actives, are meant for and should stay on the skins surface; you don't want them to penetrate through multiple layers of skin because they need to protect the skins surface. Also, lots of ingredients can propel through skin and cause beneficial changes along the way, such as most antioxidants, glycerin, sodium hyaluronate, ceramides, retinol, and numerous other repairing ingredients whose daily use helps improve skins appearance and healthy functioning. In essence, Lancomes claim makes LR 2412 sound innovative, when its really nothing new or all that exciting. But the ballyhoo sure makes it tempting!

On the ingredient list for Visionnaire, LR 2412 is listed as sodium tetrahydrojasmonate, which, as mentioned, is derived from the jasmine plant. Part of the original formula but now gone is another part of the jasmine plant, tetrahydrojasmonic acid. Both of these ingredients, in their natural state, are lipids (fats) that help the jasmine plant signal when repair is needed and that control the life cycle of the plants cells (Sources: Plant Physiology, April 2010, pages 19401950; and PLoS Biology, September 2008, page e320).

Lancome wants you to believe that these lipids, which in the jasmine plant repair environmental damage and control cell behavior, can somehow have similar effects on your skin, such as improving wrinkles, reducing large pores, and fading red marks when applied to skin via their bioengineered LR 2412 molecule. Unfortunately, there isn't a shred of published research to support their assertion. More to the point, even if these jasmine-derived ingredients were miracle workers for wrinkles, large pores, and red marks from acne, the amount of alcohol in the formula (it's the fourth ingredient) likely will harm your skin in the process, so any potential benefit is muted.

LHA another important ingredient in this product stands for lipo hydroxyl acid, which it turns out is a derivative for salicylic acid.  As someone who has combination skin, this is perfect ingredient for my skin. Apparently, according to another article, LHA is 6x more potent than salicylic acid.

Input: Recently, I was sent two different Calvin Klein colognes to review. Being both busy and lazy, as well as eager to give both colognes equal treatment, I spent two weeks with my left half doused liberally in CK One, while I drenched my right half in Obsession for Men. Here are the results!

First, much less nausea than I expected. In fact, none nausea. They both pass test number one.

Next, my initial preference is immediately for CK One. Obsession smells like if baby powder grew up into man powder. It smells like a dentist's waiting room if it were also a Baptist church full of freshly showered senior citizens. Over the past two weeks, my right side got mostly "meh"s from the men I hit on. The women I hit on with my right side were more receptive, but not my much. None of this is conclusive; I haven't tried hitting on anyone in a long time, so I'm out of practice.

I also found that Obsession for Men was far too easy to over-apply. I know I previously joked about dousing myself in the stuff, but in actuality I apply cologne by spritzing it in the air and walking through the cloud, so it's less potent than when you spray directly onto the skin.  Even with this approach, the smell was almost too strong. The smell lingers for days.

Although I preferred it, CK One still smells similar to Obsession. It's got that soft powder undertone, but it's much less pronounced in One than it is in Obsession. One is brighter, fresher, and a little fruitier. Not in a gay way (unless you're into that), but in the pineapple and papaya in the top notes. After looking up the notes for both fragrances, I think the baby powder odor must be coming from the musk and amber that both colognes have in their base notes. It makes sense that these two smell a little similar because they have many of the same components (Bergmot in the top notes, nutmeg in the heart notes, and the two aforementioned scents in the base notes).

Anyway, I preferred the CK One to Obsession, although both left the linger of powder hanging on me for days. Like that Shower-to-Shower talcum stuff my grandmother used to use all the time. A clean if not terribly sexy scent.

Input: This works o.k. for a fake tan, and does look like you've gotten some time in the sun, but it's a lot of work and time to apply. Mine came with a mitt for review purposes, but I understand that a mitt is not included when you buy the Xen-Tan. However, it wasn't all that easy to use and I think just using a plastic glove and a soft washcloth will do just as well.

I applied this thoroughly over my freshly showered bod using small circular motions as instructed in the directions. That took a while and I was working up a sweat just doing that, which caused me to have to re-apply in some spots. I couldn't do my back but I was able to smear enough on it so it was actually a good indicator of how much Xen-Tan stayed on after showering later on. I noticed I did look noticeably darker after applying the Xen-Tan. I wore loose clothing for the rest of the day and actually did not shower again until the next morning so I certainly left it on for the minimum 3 hours before showering.

When I got into the shower I saw the water run dark-ish down the drain and it had to be the Xen-Tan. I checked my back in the mirror and saw where some of the Xen-Tan had not washed off, but it was a lot lighter than when I initially applied it. I'm not really sure I'd want to spend $65.00 to work that hard, and not get much to show for it. I want to mention, that yesterday when I first applied the Xen-Tan, it felt sticky and I felt sticky for about an hour until it began to dry. Also, when I washed my hands any water that dribbled down my arms erased the Xen-Tan and I had to re-apply it. It doesn't tell you that water will erase the tan shortly after applying.  And be real careful with it on your feet because it will look like you just walked through red clay mud if you don't smear it around well.

Input: SECOND UPDATE:It's now September of 2013 and it is still working fine. Upgraded it's rating from 3 stars to 4 stars.

UPDATE: IT'S LASTED A YEAR. I'm happy it's lasted, however: During cold weather, I leave the holster at home and carry the phone + case in a coat pocket, so the holster has had several months of non-use. When I do wear the holster, I am very careful with it (after reading other reviews), especially making sure that it does not get entangled with a vehicle seat belt.

Oh, some don't like the hole in the case that reveals the iPhone's Apple logo. The hole is actually covered by transparent plastic mounted on the inside of the case, so there is some protection there.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I used Seidio holsters on my old Treo700p phone for years. They generally lasted over a year before breaking. I realized the iPhone holster will necessarily be smaller than the Treo holster, but was unpleasantly surprised at how tiny the clip is. No wonder so many reviewers report it breaks within a short time. The clip has to be narrow to fit between the iPhone's headphone jack and the on/off switch, but they could have made the clip, and the lip of the holster that it attaches to, thicker and used a larger spring. I like the look and feel and it does what it's supposed to do, as long as it doesn't break. I'd give it 4 stars (1 star off for being overpriced), but with an obvious design defect that Seidio must be aware of from all the user feedback, and chooses to do nothing about, I give it 3 stars and will try to treat it very gingerly.

Input: Probably a 3 1/2 star vs 4, but since I had to choose, I chose 4.  Here is the lowdown:

1) Did tons of research, mostly online but also at a local Best Buy.  The best buy only had one pair of blue tooth stereo headphones period, and the sales kid (I do stress "kid") told me "This is the only pair we have in stock right now and these are the only ones on the market...no one else even sells one"  of course theirs were $149 and they would not let me try them out.  Also considered motorola, HK, samsung, and others.

2)  According to C-Net, amazon, bizrate, and others these were consistently the best performers rated for bluetooth headphones...amazon had the best price, even over bizrate, ebay, etc.

3)  Got the headphones in a very timely manner (it helps to live within one day delivery for supersaver shipping...heh heh heh) and set them up very easily for my wife to use with her new samsung cell phone to listen to tunes from the micro SD card.

4)  SHE LOVES THEM....they work well in high-noise environments (the gym) they have enough volume, intuitive controls that are easily accessible and the bluetooth connection is strong.  One of my worries was the fact that they were rechargable and how long a charge would last.  She used them until they literally died before recharging and it resulted in over 10 days total - turning them off when not in use, then with a solid 4-5 hours of playback time, about 1 hour a day every other day.  I imagine if you kept them on all the time and/or used the playback constantly it would likely give you 7 hours+ of playback time at relatively high volume.  Good performance.

5)  Here is the downside...they only fit medium sized people (if that is the right phrase).  I am 6'2" and large-ish (ok, 260 lbs).  The behind the neck band, which works great for my supermodel-ish wife only works for me if I keep my head down, staring into my lap.  If I move my head or look up (or even straight ahead for that matter) the neck band pulls the ear-pads off my ears enough to mess with the music.  Not a good thing.  Someone needs to come up with a neck band that is adjustable and will work for larger than average sized folks.

6)  #5 above and the fact that the headphones lack a very broad dynamic range (somewhat tinny highs, muted mids, not very low lows) is why I downgraded this to a 3 1/2 to 4 stars, but really the music quality I would rate just below Very Good and the fit and comfort, for my wife at least, is exemplary.

Nice job Cardo, now fix the head band and get a stronger driver and you will have a perfect set of headphones.

Input: While charging the Energizer device it displays four large flashing blue light bars.  It is easy to see when the device has a complete charge since all four bars will be illuminated and no longer flash.  Pretty cool that the light bars work the same way when you draw from the device to another piece of electronics and the bars stopped flashing when my iPhone had a full charge.  Since I already had a household plug (AC) to USB adapter, this was easy to utilize; however, I am sure some would prefer a charger that just simply plugged directly into the wall.  The advantage of the device with the current design is one could plug it into a USB port on their computer or laptop and charge the charger (or items connected to it..although not at the same time).

It has enough juice to recharge my iPhone 4S twice over (from 15% left each time and it took around 2.5 hours each time) and then had some juice some left over.  It allows you to charge two devices at once and even has one of the two USB connections configured to charge your tablet [although the instructions warn for some people you might not be able to charge two devices at once (depending on the wattage of the devices)].  You can charge a tablet and a cell phone at the same time; however, cannot charge two tablets at the same time. I didn't have great luck charging my iPad from a depleted level; however, it worked fine on the iPhone and the specs on this are consistent with those results.  The micro USB cable that attaches to charge the device is magnetized so as to facilitate keeping it with the charger at all times to avoid misplacing it.  I also like the soft rubber exterior as that helps if it is bumping against other expensive electronics in a bag.  When not charging the device one could use the micro USB cable to attach to devices with that type of connection (which is great since several devices use that); however, you will need your Apple cord to accompany this device when charging Apple products.

While the device is fairly compact, it is also fairly heavy.  While this is a testament to its build quality (and purpose) other devices offer higher capacity at a smaller size and wieght. I don't know how practical it will be for some to carry this around regularly in a briefcase, purse or travel bag.  However, it is really handy when you know you will be in a remote area or outside and not around a power source for an extended period of time.  Or, this is great if one has a long flight or long layover in an airport without power sources.  Plus, the true value of this product can obviously be seen when one loses power in their home for an extended period of time.  I am in the suburbs of New York City and when Hurricane Sandy hit we lost power for several days.  This was a lifesaver as I had recently received this item just a few weeks before the storm and had an opportunity to charge it (took five hours out of the box to charge) and have it ready to go.  Note, once depleted it took me a bit over six hours to get the Energizer back to four bars and a full charge.  Plus, while I did not have power for several days, I was able to travel a short distance to relatives and not just recharge my electronic devices, but also this device to serve as a backup between charges.

Bottom line, this does what it is supposed to do and I already benefitted from its use on a number of occasions and will do so in the future as well.  However, I think this device is a bit pricey based on its size, weight and capacity compated to other devices on the market.

Input: Placing a mount on the vents is the most optimal position you can put your phone in the car - suction cups will always lose their stickiness and fall off, freaking you out every time. It also doesn't block any view from your windshield. That's why I really like the minimalist simplicity of the device as far as air vent mounts go. There's no risk of it falling off or plopping down, causing you another mini-heart attack and risking a car accident. Downsides to this though - you can't turn the phone away/towards you side-to-side. It only rotates 360 degrees in a circle in a 2D plane (if that makes sense, you can see it in other video reviews here).

Also, the clip did not secure to the vent as tightly as I expected it to. I think it works best with vents that aren't curved but rather for vents that are straight and flat. I think it worked better in a 2014 Mazda CX5 than a 2010 Toyota Corolla. As a result of this, it can't really handle fairly large phones such as the Huawei Ascend Mate 2 (slightly larger than the iPhone 6 PLUS and Galaxy Note's). That Huawei is probably as big as a phone gets before getting to phablet territory, so I can't really fault it for not working on one of the largest phones out there. When the mount latched on to this phone, it would clamp down/hit the power and volume buttons on the sides, and when we tried to place it away from these side buttons, the weight of the phone pushed to one side would make it slip and fall off the mount.

It worked serviceably well for my old Samsung Galaxy SII though, so the smaller the phone the more stable it is on the mount. So if it works/fits in your car vent and you don't have a huge-butt phone, this mount is really great for the price!

Input: It's great! The screen is crystal clear. It goes on fairly easy. They could have kept that cheap microfiber cloth though... that thing left mores dust than it picked up. I wasn't expecting a whole lot for a $4 glass screen to protect my Galaxy Note 4 but I am thoroughly impressed. People take note, it will not cover the entire  face of your phone. The device has curved edges so it's pretty much impossible to cover the entire face of your phone without it peeling up on the sides. However this screen does an awesome job of protecting the viewable area. Because of the curvature of the phone it makes it tricky to install. Take your time!!! What I did was place the screen on the phone (without removing the cover that exposes the adhesive), lined it up where I needed it to be, and then taped one side of the screen to the phone itself, almost like creating a book cover. This keeps the screen in place. Then I lifted the screen (like opening a book),  pulled the back of the screen off (exposing the adhesive) and gently closed it down on the screen. It's lined almost perfectly. There's no air bubbles. Pull the tape off and it's good to go!  I hope my review helps. I'll definitely be recommending this to my friend....

**update 4/3/15**
OK so a day after I wrote the above review, the stupid thing spontaneously cracked along the side. I've never dropped the phone or even sat it down hard anywhere.. I guess u get what you pay for....

Input: I bought this case in 2 colors, the white & the aqua.  I used the white for about a year before switching to the aqua, also for a year, & never had any problems, although I never dropped my phone on anything other than grass or carpet.

The fit was excellent for my Note 4, the ports were easily accessible, & the buttons pressed perfectly. I liked the color & style.

However. I'm giving these cases 2 stars because they failed to do what they claim: protect my phone.

Just a couple weeks ago,  while standing, I stuck my phone under my arm while trying to close my purse (bad idea) and my phone fell approximately 4 feet, flat on its face, on the sidewalk.
Right away I thought,  pssshhhhh, my phone will be fine... it's protected by an Otterbox & a high-end tempered glass screen protector!
Boy, was I wrong.

I picked up the phone & saw 2 hairline cracks on the lower half of my tempered glass. When I pressed the power key, the screen stayed black. The phone rang, but I couldn't use the screen to answer it. That night, I plugged it into the charger & felt the vibration feedback. Phone continued to ring as I received calls.

The next day, the phone no longer rang or buzzed. I tried calling it from another phone & nothing. I removed the screen protector & saw some cracks.

I'm extremely disappointed that the Otterbox, even backed up by tempered glass, did not protect my phone.  When I got a Note 8 to replace my beloved Note 4, I decided I would not be buying another Otterbox case. I read a bunch of reviews & watched a bunch of videos & decided on the Tech21 Evo Check. It's not available on Amazon as far as I know,  so I bought the white one from Tech21's website & the black one from BestBuy. I also bought the Whitestone Dome tempered glass (available on Amazon). Hopefully these new cases & screen protector will protect my phone better than those Otterbox Commuters.

Input: I'm usually wary of skins/wraps for my devices, and with good reason: they generally suck. That said, I grew tired of my bulky OtterBox case and decided to give one of these a try. I figured that in the 5+ years since I've bothered to try a skin, there MUST have been some advances in execution. Right?

Wrong!

Right off the bat, I noticed a half-crescent dent in the bottom of the back panel due to the idiotic way it is packaged. Secondly, it does NOT fit correctly. The cut-outs do not quite line up and one piece was actually too long, resulting in an overlap. For triple the price of what I could have gotten on eBay, I really expected better. I expected it to not look quite so cheap and to, I don't know, fit my phone. Finally, it did leave bubbles, etc. no matter how painstakingly I tried to apply these ill-fitting stickers. The only product claim that was true was that it didn't leave residue when I removed it from my phone to send back.

Avoid this product like the plague. I normally wouldn't bother returning such an inexpensive item, but in this case it was a matter of principle.

Input: After reading reviews and watching the installation videos on YouTube, I understood there would be imperfections that should clear up in time, and I am finding that to be true.  As suggested by a reviewer I did the installation in a bathroom after steaming it up to settle any dust particles.

The front cover installation was fairly easy.
I ran out of solution before getting to the back cover and was told by customer service to just add a little water to the bottle, and that worked. (I think I used too much to wet my fingers.)

The back cover is harder to install. It takes a bit or work to get all the cutouts for the camera, speakers and buttons lined up. The corners have to be nearly dry before they are tacky enough to stay down, so just leave them alone until then. The video did not include back cover installation, which would have been helpful.

There were streaks and bubbles initially, but here on day 2, most of these, including a quarter inch water bubble that was trapped over the Apple logo, have all but disappeared.

The screen appearance is crystal clear and finger prints and smudges are much less noticeable than on the bare screen.

When/if the bubbles completely clear up I will update my review.

I also received a coupon code for an additional screen protector shipped free,  which was a nice surprise!

Update: This update is long overdue, but I'm changing my rating to 3 stars, because the bubbles and imperfections never completely cleared up. I lived with it for a while and recently installed the complimentary one that I received. The result was even worse!  I really wanted this to work because it does provide good protection and I loved that it did not show fingerprints.  I gave in and bought a dry installed one instead.  I am leaving the back protector on though, because I don't have to look at it.
