Input: This review is for the Innogie Air Thin 6600mAh Portable Charger External Battery Pack, Power Bank & iPhone Charger for iPhone, iPad and Samsung Galaxy and More (Pink)

Received this product and immediately charged it to 100%. I then charged a Galaxy Tab S 8.4". The tablet has a 4,900 mAh battery. The starting charge on the Tab S was 24%.

Device  Capacity  Start  % To Full  mAh used  Efficiency %
Tab S  4,900  24%  76%  3,724  57%  Power bank (PB) depleted.

Definitely not the best efficiency of all the batteries I own, but possibly acceptable. I will try a few more runs to see what the numbers add up to.
-The battery and tablet became warmer than when using other power banks (output of 1 and 2 amp). Not too hot that it worried me, but I feel that too much power is lost to this heat.
-There is no flashlight (which I prefer, regardless of brightness). If you have ever been in a blackout at night, ANY amount of light will be useful! -The build is nice and sturdy.
-Very nice looking aluminum housing. Another reviewer mentioned sharp edges, I did not not have this on my unit.
-The indicator lights for power level will only turn on when a charging cable is attached.
  --Checking on the current status of the PB is inconvenient.
-My wife really likes the size and color of the PB

I ordered this for its size. My wife liked another brand's size (but with very poor efficiency) because she could stack her Galaxy S4 on top and hold both while talking on the phone. I bought this hoping to satisfy her wish for a similar sized power bank.

I will update this review after doing a few more tests,

===== Update on Efficiency : =====
I have used the Innogie three times from full to depleted. The efficiency percentage has been 73%,54%, and 55%. If the PB does not get at least 60% efficiency, I will be requesting a return authorization.
===Edit==
I really am feeling a little leery that you cannot check the power level of the battery without having to plug in a charging cable. That is feeling like a deal breaker.

Input: Android KitKat made some changes to how apps can use the SD card.  Unfortunately Google didn't give any of the app developers enough warning to adapt.  So, if you need to use an SD card stay away from KitKat.

With KitKat apps have very limited use of the SD card.  They can only write to restricted areas.  This is supposedly for security, but it's nonsense because the internal memory works freely.  This makes it so any app that used to write to the SD card is either broken or writing to internal memory.  Some developers may be able to adapt their apps to handle this issue, but that kind of development takes time.  More time than it would take Google to snap out of it and stop blocking SD card writing.  Not really a problem for Google Nexus users who don't have an SD card slot ...

Here's where the Moto G comes in:  The LTE version of the Moto G comes with KitKat and there is no older version you can flash back to.  So if you buy the Moto G LTE you are stuck with KitKat.  For that reason, I don't recommend the LTE version of this phone.

Unless rooting this phone will fix the issue I'm basically stuck with a brick and I'm back to my old phone.  It's a shame, because the Moto G worked so nice and smooth.  I would 100% recommend this phone if there was a way to get KitKat off of it.  I may update this review after I've rooted the phone.  If this problem can be fixed with simple rooting it would be more fair to give the phone more stars, but people should really be warned about this because not everybody can or should root their phones.

A Google-friendly explanation of the issue is at this link:
http://www.androidcentral.com/kitkat-sdcard-changes?pg=4#content

Input: I was intrigued by the design and was in need of a new micro USB cable, so I gave this product a shot. The product came with a pretty nice package which included one micro USB cable, two metal plugs, and a plastic plank (to assist with taking the metal plug off from the device). I was quite excited and happy with my purchase at first, but after testing it out for a couple days, I realized how inconvenient this product really is. Below are the lists of pros and cons I found.
Pros:
1. There are two metal plugs. Didn't really affect me since I only needed it for my phone. Would be nice for people w/ phone and tablet or other devices.
2. The metal plug fit in the Micro USB jack perfectly. It clicked in tightly so I didn't have to worry about losing the tiny piece of metal plate.
3. The magnet worked well. It wouldn't come off easily when charging.

Cons:
1. The biggest problem I had with this product was that I had to bring this specific cable with me all the time if I wanna charge my phone when I was out. The metal plug fit in the jack so well that it's almost impossible to unplug it bare handed. When I forgot to bring the cable (and the plank to unplug the metal plug) with me to work, I couldn't charge my phone even there was a regular micro usb cable I could use...
2. It charged SO SLOWLY. Probably slower than charging w/ regular micro usb cable on a laptop.
3. The plastic plank is quite soft. I was struggling a little bit when using the plank to take the metal plug off from my phone. The front part of the plank already has some dents after being used only once.

At this moment I am going back to my old micro USB cable.
I like the design and the concept of the product; however, it is too inconvenient for me to use.

*Disclaimer: I received this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review.*

Input: I like to tinker with random projects in the garage, and for some reason, I really like to tinker with 12 volt electrical projects. Bring on the 120 piece Cal-Hawk variety pack!

The fuses came in a plastic case that leaves a lot to be desired.  The case has very cheap clasps and I broke one off after the second time I opened it.  The amperage rating on the fuses is very hard to read unless you get the correct angle or happen to be looking at the key on the box itself.  Those two minor issues aside, if you go to the hardware store and buy a 4 pack of blade fuses, they cost about a buck, so it's easy to see the value in this large 120 pack.

I also appreciate the variety of amperages the package comes in.  I have plenty to chose from for my custom wiring jobs and also all the standard amp sizes for my vehicles.  If you've ever blown an auto fuse before and had to run to the hardware store for a single fuse, you know how much of a time saver this will be.  5 stars for the value and variety, but go easy on the flimsy storage box so you don't play a game of 120 fuse pick-up!

Input: The front end portion of this install went fairly well with only a couple of issues. The rear end was another story. I had to drill out the female side of the aluminum blocks in order for them to fit onto the axle/spring pack. Definitely get the longer unbolts but make sure that when you call to order them the guy on the other end of the line hears you correctly. My guy sent me unbolts that were about 1.5 inches to long. I had to cut them in order to be able to get my deep socket onto the nut. You will need these because the stock ones are only long enough to get a couple of turns with your ratchet. Threadlock or no threadlock that is not enough for me. Get ahold of your dealer to get the correct torque specs for your nuts and bolts. When I called their tech support I was initially told 110# for the rear end ubolt nuts. That didn't sound right so I had him check with an installer. He came back with 140#. That sounded closer but I called the dealer and for my application I needed to torque mine to 160#. Don't forget to get your torque specs for your front spring perches. There are no torque specs provided in the install instructions for any of your parts. Also the rear shock extender instructions are horrible. Tech support could not provide any clarity so I didn't use them and my truck is just fine. The ride was not affected. The end result the kit did what it is suppose to do. My truck is level and looks great. If you have a buddy that can spare a portion of their day don't shy about asking. I did mine by myself and it was work. Your alignment guy may suggest a camber kit to get you dead on. So far I have not had any problems with tire wear because the variance was so slight. Have fun and good luck.

Input: I bought this unit specifically as a mid watt power source in case of 9/11 shenanigans. It arrived at my place in a box and appeared well packaged. It would not start. I then went forth with diagnostics. As with any engine check fuel, air and spark first if it won't start. Turns out it was delivered with a broken spark plug. Started right up when I replaced it. Runs well with synthetic 2 cycle oil 50 to 1. Does exactly what its advertised to do- 800 w continuous, 1250w for short bursts. It will run a 12 amp circular saw for short jobs. Except for a stripped handle screw, no other problems. I recommend this product only for people with some mechanical knowledge. If you buy it make sure it works immediately! If you save it unused for an emergency you may be unpleasantly surprised, or if you take it camping without tools or parts.

Input: I wanted to give them a 5 star rating after I installed the passenger side until they DID NOT fit on the drivers side and I wanted to give them 1 star - the average is 3 stars.  Dorman claims these fit perfect.  They do, but only one side of your vehicle!  When something only fits on one side - its DOESN'T fit on the other side!  I replaced the seat heater pads on the seat bottom and seat back.  I ordered both Dorman parts (641-105 & 641-106) through Amazon.  Obviously with Amazon, great price, great shipping, etc.  Check out the You Tube video(s) I will upload shortly (under 'debandpete') on the actual problem/process with these.  One side went in without problems.  There are tons of videos on You Tube and instructions with the seat heater pad.  The problem is that since they are 'universal' and the wire does not come out of the seat heater pad in the middle - it comes out on one, which means that on one side of your vehicle it will reach the connecting electrical coupler underneath the seat, BUT on the other side of the vehicle it will not reach.  There are people that suggest pulling the supplied 'sticky tape' off and putting it on the other side.  DO NOT do this.  The seat heater pads are directional and designed to heat mostly in one direction.  If you look at the design close enough, you will see that.  The instructions even tell you to not put the tape side up to the upholstery.  If you flip the pad over and put the tape on what was the top and is now facing down, the heat will be going into the foam and not into you.  The answer ended-up being to simply route the electrical cord out the opposite side that the factory cable was routed through.  If both the seat bottom pad & seat back pad are both on the wrong side, then they will still plug into each other as designed and still reach the GM connector under thereat frame.  Sounds simple but wasted a lot of time, phone calls and of course happens on the weekend when Dorman was closed.  Dorman SHOULD add a simple paragraph to their instructions explaining this process.  Check out my You Tube video shortly!

Input: At the top of Amazon's description page of any automotive part, a pop-up will come on and state: "Make sure it fits" your vehicle.  DON"T RELY ON THIS INFORMATION!!  In this case, Amazon's information showed that this window visor DID fit my Ford Ranger.  When it arrived, I took it out of the box and it became obvious that it was way too large for the windows for my Ford Ranger.  Upon reviewing the shipping information on the box, it was for a full size Ford 150 pickup.  I contacted the manufacturer to request information and found that the correct manufacturing number for the items to fit my Ranger was EGR 563041.  I returned the items to Amazon and am currently awaiting for Amazon to provide me with the full purchase price on my credit card.  I then ordered the deflectors, through Amazon, utilizing the correct manufacturer's provided number.  I got an excellent price, got free shipping, and they arrived quickly.  Unfortunately, when they arrived, they were broken in the package-apparently by UPS.  I will write a separate review on that item. I have found that several items I was interested in purchasing (in the automotive section) had incorrect information provided through the Make Sure it Fits info provided by Amazon.  If you are interested, definitely keep Amazon in mind for their pricing and delivery, but conduct your own research through the manufacturer's website or by phone contact. Input: The saddest Bilstein shocks I have ever experienced...

As a long time motorcycle and performance car enthusiast, I am very familiar with what suspension should and should not do. These shocks have a MAJOR lack of rebound dampening, they feel as if they have 300,000 miles on them and do not control the car at all. It will require a revalving with about 30-40% more rebound dampening, for a stock 1992 Caprice wagon. I do not load my car, it is a commuter, it stays clean and empty at all times besides the fuel tank.

While these shocks may be okay on a sedan with 140-160 lb/inch springs, the wagon has a 211lb/inch rear springs, and is not controlled sufficiently with these shocks despite all claims that they are "stiff" and or "performance oriented."  Do not believe the hype on the forums, these WILL require a revalve to match the feel of their front Bilstein shock counterparts on a wagon. The compression dampening however is nearly perfect.

Input: The good: nice to have a screen, full featured, looks good in my car, plays music :)

The bad: the volume is quiet, even on full.  The screen is small and things like track numbers are even smaller and a poor color choice, so it's difficult/impossible to read while you're driving.  It does not have an input jack, so only works as a standalone player.  Worst of all, the instructions are worthless and the controls are not intuitive.  I discovered the following by trial and error over 2 months of frustration:

(>/=)
- tap once to pause/play
- hold down two seconds to turn off
- tap twice to turn on

(VOL)
- tap once to adjust the volume with the up/down arrows
- tap again to adjust the frequency with the up/down arrows

(M)
- While playing, tap once to get to the repeat/equalizer menu
- While paused, tap once to go to the folder menu
- hold down two seconds to select music/movie/jpg mode

(|<<)
- while playing, tap to skip back a song
- hold to rewind while playing
- while paused, tap to skip back a folder

(>>|)
- while playing, tap to skip fwd a song
- hold to rewind while playing
- while paused, tap to skip ahead a folder

If you unplug it (or remove power) while a track is playing, it will start over at the start of the track when power is restored.
If you turn it off by holding the play button, and then remove/depower it, it will start over in the middle of the track.
If you enter a track # with the remote, it will skip right to that track.

The new filter has a cardboard type edge only on two opposing sides, and the other two sides are merely the filter element.  This can cause a less than perfect seal and allow air to pass thru these edge of the filter.  Now don't get me wrong, I don't believe a cabin air filter does much more than catch acorns and grasshoppers anyway, but the sealing properties of this one are not as good as the one I had.

As far as the fit is concerned, the dimensions are correct to fit my car and it does fit well--minus the issue I describe above.  If Purolator would put the same type of stiff edge around the entire filter assembly instead of just on two sides, this would be a much better filter.

Input: So first of all some product specifcations:

Battery life = 600 mAh (fills my iphone 3Gs which is about 1200 mAh half way)

There is one mini usb port on it that acts as both a power in and power out. The device comes with a bunch of mini-usb adapters to allow you to connect various other devices to the charger's mini usb.

There is a single button on the device, if you press it once, the green light will blink indicating that it will output power to anything you connect, and if you press the button twice, the flashlight will turn on.

Review:

I had intended to use this to be a little bit greener and allow me to run my Iphone 3Gs off of solar energy. The first day, I had it sit in the sun for a while and when it was in the sun, the little red light would turn on indicating that it was charging. When it got dark, i decided to charge my dead iphone battery, and it got to 50% charge and then the charger ran out of juice.

That night, I placed the device in my window intending to have it charge all the next day. When I woke up, the device's red light was blinking, and the flashlight was on, but not very bright. I tried pushing the button, but nothing was happening. So I decided to give it a little wall charge for a second. After that the device behaved normally. So I placed it back in the sun, and saw the red light come back on.

At the end of the day, I checked up on it, and yet again, the device had the blinking red light and the flashlight was on. The charger battery was basically completely empty, and could not charge my iphone at all.

The bottom line:

When you connect the device to the wall, the charger works fine and as it should (however, the battery does not last very long). However when you try to use the sun to charge.. just forget it. I wouldn't recommend buying this product.

Input: For now I'll leave four stars due to my scepticism on have an LED controller running at 84+ degrees Celsius (184F) without expect that will fail.
I'm definitely satisfied with the results on change a pair of HID for these LEDs. Measured brightness before and after shows that this LEDs are far more bright.
However I also took several temperature measurements which scares me and you can see on my attached pictures.
The main controller reached that temperature in just 10 minutes. Reading some other customers reviews I decided to stick an aluminum heat sink in order to try to cool this module and may have some extra lifetime. I also noted that the LED bulb itself don't rise the temperature above 60 degrees Celsius (140F) due to the cooling fan "till it fail lol"..
There are two possibilities: I come back here in six months and rise this review to 5 stars or near between come here with my failure analysis.
Just for comparison, one image shows my fog light from Syrius (LED) and the head light slight more blue.
The last thermal image is an interesting comparison of heat signature of my Prius engine and on left side the bright led controller..

UPDATED:
Well, a little more than 6 months as I promised I rose to 5 stars. I'm definitely very satisfied with this Led Light and the electronic controller didn't fail. Just want to reinforce that the usage here is about 4 hous/day mean, and often used for more than 2 hours uninterrupted.
One thing I noted (and expected) is that the fans where gone, both fans died but this is not affecting the lights neither the max temperature. Probably there is a thermistor on the LED to slight reduce the current to lower the temperature "my guess".

UPDATED2:
Less than 1000hrs of life one unit surprisingly had its LED module burned despite of my efforts on maintain the driver cool. Attached the dead module side which caused the entire unit to fail as well a tear down picture. I did some tests on the driver (simple swap) and it's still working, as well I did a test on the internal fan which is also working. So, after tear down I was surprised to see that the module don't have ANY temperature management on its LED boards or the entire heatsink block. Of course, lack of temperature management or current management is the root cause of 90% of premature death of high power LED devices. I'm taking 3 stars out, one for my disappointment, one for the lack of temperature management and another for the lie on their advertises which states "monitor the fan speed to get the best temperature protection", the fan installed is a simple unmanaged 6v fan, there is no sensor to reduce the power on the LED when the fan is manually blocked making the unit reach incredible high temperatures in just a few minutes.

Input: Excruciating experience with the Bertazzoni service. We bought a Bertazzoni gas range Master 30" a year ago. The week before Easter of this year the oven ignition broke down. It is now mid-May and it has yet to be fixed! They kept saying that the needed part will be mailed overnight to the company servicing the range and that we'll have it fixed over the next couple of days. I just talked to them and was told that the part is back-ordered and they can not do anything about it! Really? It will be 6 weeks by then! After insisting that they get it fixed asap and after being put on hold I am told that they "found" the part. It remains to be seen if indeed we will have a working oven soon...

Now about the performance of this range: first, the range looks good! Second, the top burners are fine especially when you need high heat. My only complaint is that the simmering is not performing well. Even with the simmering ring there is way too much heat for a slow cooking stew in a Dutch oven. My solution: I pile two grates such that the Dutch oven stays high enough. The downside: it looks ridiculous and I can not use the other burners! The oven: works fine for cooking/braising meat which requires more moisture but not so well for baking which can not be turned and therefore gets burnt on the bottom. My solution for this was to place a metal tray underneath such that the heat gets diffused and circulates better (this happens even with the fan on). Bottom line: first, appliances sometimes break down and that is fine but then the service should be of quality and prompt; second, for the price this range should work without these rather embarrassing adjustments! I have made an effort to like this range, hence the adjustments, but the service I have received so far really sealed my thoughts on the Bertazzoni, and they are not positive!

Input: My wife and I use both the stove top and the oven quite a lot. We generally like the way the stove looks, and the stove top works well after a couple of service visits to get the high power middle burner working properly. But the oven heats very unevenly and it's a huge pain to light the oven without having the flame go out.

The stove top burners generally work well, but we had trouble from the beginning with the dual-burner in the middle. We could generally get the outer ring started, and the inner ring would ignite but then would go out as soon as we let go of its ignition knob. It took two visits from the service company to get the burner adjusted to work properly. The high power burner is great for getting a big pot of water boiling quickly for pasta.

The oven, however, is a problem. The first thing we realized is that there was no temperature read-out. We already had our own thermometer, which we hung on the back wall of the oven, but it is obviously much less convenient to read this than if Bertazzoni had installed an LED readout somewhere on the front panel. Obviously the oven knows what the temperature is, because the oven is good at maintaining a steady level; why couldn't Bertazzoni figure out a nice way to display this?

The next thing we noticed (and the manual warns of this) is that after lighting the oven burner, you have to close the oven door very slowly to keep the flame from blowing out. When the flame blows out without our noticing it, we get natural gas leaking into the kitchen, not a nice thing at all. And it's not easy to close the oven door slowly, because, as with most ranges, there is a spring built into the door close mechanism.

Finally, the "convection" feature is kind of a joke. I had really looked forward to this feature, as we do a moderate amount of baking. But cookies, bread, and Thanksgiving turkey all get cooked extremely unevenly. We pulled our turkey out of the oven prematurely because one side read 170 degrees. The other side was bloody. We're admittedly rookies at cooking big birds (this was 13 pounds) but this was pretty unbelievable.

We like the stove top quite a lot, but wish we could have a different oven, ideally an electric one. Unfortunately, we're in a building with an old electrical system and it would have cost a fortune to bring more power to our 11th floor apartment.  So we've learned to watch our cookies closely, rotate them frequently, and remove individual cookies before they burn. Next time we cook a turkey we'll cut it into pieces ahead of time, rotate it frequently, and hope for better results.

Input: I have had this dishwasher installed for 3 loads now. Runs excellent. Extremely quiet. Manages to get dishes cleaned without pre-washing. Drying is typical of a Bosch from other reviews I have read, but works well for me. THE ONLY ISSUE IS BEST BUY / PACIFIC KITCHENS AND THEIR INSTALLERS!
Starting with the pre-measure procedure. There didn't seem to be any communication from the start. The installers got there ready to measure for an electric range, not a dishwasher. That got fixed. Then the day for install came. Appliance came in damaged, delivery was refused and the new dishwasher was taken away but the old one left in place. This was on a Saturday and a new delivery day was made for the following Wednesday. Saturday night I received an email with an Installation Control Form attached, basically saying that the old dishwasher was hauled away and the new one was installed and I knew about the damage, but accepted it anyway. On this form, someone printed my name on all of the appropriate lines, as if to forge my signature. I know it wasn't me because I was out of town for Army Reserves training and it wasn't my mother on my behalf (she was the one to refuse delivery). Monday came and I received another email stating they were coming Wednesday to haul away the old dishwasher but made no mention of the new dishwasher. I called and was told it was on backorder. After a lot of back and forth I managed to get a new delivery day of the following Monday. That Monday came and I finally received my dishwasher.
I will never buy from Pacific Kitchens again.....and I'm truly contemplating not ever going back into Best Buy for any reason. As I said in the title....You should definitely buy this dishwasher, but I would get it from a company that will not lie to you or try forging your signature on documents.

Input: So I bought this dishwasher from my local appliance store's "floor model" section. I was without a dishwasher, had a house full of dirty dishes, and was about to be snowed in so I took a chance. I hadn't checked the Amazon reviews, maybe I would have decided on something else if I had.

First of all, my thoughts on price - this is NOT a $1000 dishwasher. I would never have paid that much for it. It is a perfectly good $500 dishwasher, which is what I paid. I could really see people being disgruntled if they had paid a lot for this unit.

This is, in spite of its price tag and appearance, a pretty mid-grade dishwasher in terms of features and performance - hence me being happy with the $500 price tag.

I want to address some of the common complaints I've seen on here:

Complaint: The handle hits the floor.
My Take: No, it doesn't. Where did you mount this? You would have to shove the front door all the way past fully open. Huh? The door doesn't hard-stop at horizontal, is that what you mean?

Complaint: Racks are unwieldy/fall out/come off the rails/etc.
My Take: Top rack has been rock solid. Bottom rack isn't actually ON rails, and the door does go past horizontal so ... but seriously? I haven't ever had a problem.

Complaint: No heating element.
My Take: It pretty much says in BIG BOLD LETTERS that it doesn't have a heating element. Really? You bought a Ford and you're complaining it doesn't have a twin turbo in it? Umm... yeah.

Complaint: Funny smell.
My Take: The first few washes I ran there was a "new dishwasher, hot plastic/rubber/metal" smell. It got better and better with each load until it went away. Occasional stink is handled with DISHWASHER CLEANER. You do know they make that, right? Of course you do.

Complaint: It's slow.
My Take: As compared to...?

Complaint: Fills with water.
My Take: It's a dish... washer. It fills with water. That's what it does.

But seriously now, here's my thoughts.

Cons:

1. No heated dry. This is also a pro, so it really evens out. But if you were looking for heated dry, this isn't going to make you happy. The dishes evaporatively dry. Everything on the lower rack is good and dry, everything on the upper rack that faces downward is dry. Anything with a concave top on the upper rack will be a little damp. That's pretty much to be expected with a unit like this.

2. A limited number of fancy features. You get delicate/normal/heavy wash, rinse only, top rack wash (that's a pro, though) and child lock. That's ... pretty ... much ... it.

3. The flatware rack is a little ... limiting. Not the worst I've seen, but not even as good as my old Whirlpool.

4. No steam. It has "sani-rinse" but it's unclear exactly what that does since there's no heating element. I suspect it just makes the water VERY HOT.

Neither Pro nor Con:

1. It's slow. This is to be expected from an ultra-quiet, ultra-efficient unit. A full wash SAYS it will take 2 hours but quickly senses load and dirt levels. With normal loading in my experience it takes about 85 minutes. Not too bad, but not a speed demon.

Pro:

1. Stainless tub. Really nice.

2. Super quiet. I feel the vibration in the floor more than I hear the noise of operation. And neither is pronounced.

3. "Top rack only" option. This is the one feature I was delighted to have because I really missed it in my old Fisher/Paykel - the ability to JUST wash glasses after you've had people over for drinks or snacks... or after your teenagers have wandered in and out and made every glass you own dirty.

4. High efficiency. Limited water use.

5. No heating element. Yeah, that means no heated dry. But it also mean no melted tupperware.

6. Load and soil sensing. The unit starts with a guesstimate for time and water needed, and adjusts from there. I'm pretty impressed, actually. A heavily soiled load took 95+ minutes, more lightly soiled loads as little as 70, the average has been around 80-85.

Input: Everyone,

My wife bought me this kegerator for a birthday present and I was super excited.  I ordered a keg of Stone IPA, and after some searching, I found a local place that exchanges 5 lbs beverage-quality CO2 canisters.  I went ahead and swapped the empty that came with this setup for one of their exchange canisters because in the end, I think it will make my life easier not having to worry about refilling it.

I put it all together, let everything chill down inside the fridge to the coldest setting of 7 (this is important because the CO2 loses pressure when it gets cold).  When I went to pour the beer, it was super foamy.  I thought it was just the new keg so I let it sit for another day, and I tried it again only to end up with the same result.  I wasn't sure what to do, so I did some research and found that for my elevation, my regulator was out-of-the-box set to 25 PSI - way too high.  I found a PSI kegerator chart, and realized that I needed to be at a much, much lower PSI of around 5.  I got a wrench and twisted the +/- nob on the regulator until I got it down to 5 PSI and that solved the foam problem - I did not need a new hose like some of the reviews stated.

My next issue.  Once I adjusted the pressure the pour was fine, but I noticed the beer had a really strong plastic/rubber/metallic/chemical smell/taste.  I did more research and convinced myself I had oxidized my beer by having it exposed to too much CO2 PSI -  this later turned out to be false and I learned that beer can easily withstand up to 30 PSI without being ruined.  I was ready to call it a wasted-keg-day, but out of denial I continued to do research on the problem.

Finally, I found an article on a beer brewing forum that talked about how the synthetic washer between the keg and the tap hose could be to blame.  I disconnected the keg from the hose that connects it to the pourer, and I could smell the problem at once.  There is this white ring/washer/gasket thing that comes with this kegerator that is known to give the beer this horrible taste/smell as it passes over it and/or sits in the tube, and it reeked of that chemical smell.  I truly did not know one little washer could stink and foul up beer so badly, but it sure can.  My fingers still smelled like that chemical a day after I washed them, and I have a terrible sense of smell.  I yanked that thing out, replaced it with a rubber o-ring, and the problem was 90% solved.  I ordered a keg cleaning kit to flush the remainder of the smell out of the tap tube, and a set of black synthetic washers that has been reported not to have that problem.

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 is because of the research I had to do, and the emotional toll it took on me thinking I ruined 5 gallons of expensive beer.  I can tell you right now with 100% honesty that I am enjoying a beer, straight from my keg, and it is delicious.  This thing is going to turn me into a beer snob for sure.

I emailed the people at Smart+ and hopefully soon they will stop shipping those bad-news white washers.

Make sure you adjust your regulator, make sure you don't use one of those white washers, and you will love this thing.

-R

Input: Aqua-Pure filters are made in the US under license from the patent holder. This is a cheap Chinese knock-off of uncertain quality. Do not buy this POS if you want a real Aqua-Pure filter.

UPDATE: After seller insisted in Questions that this filter is made in the USA and only assembled in China, I decided to test it to see if his additional claim that it works as well as any other filter is true. I tested it with the TDS meter I use to monitor the RO/DI water purifier I use for my saltwater aquarium. First, I ran 5 gallons of water through this filter installed in my Samsung fridge. The water was black for a while, but it cleared up by gallon 3. Instructions say run it for 5 minutes to flush carbon dust, and it took about 7 minutes to pull 5 G.

Measured TDS for the "Aqua-Pure compatible" was 138 PPM. Then I measured unfiltered tap water, and once again got 138 PPM. I repeated the test three times on each water source and got the same figures, +/- 1 PPM.

Consequently, I know that this device does not filter water at all and is certainly not compatible with Aqua Pure. It works no better than having no filter at all in the fridge.

UPDATE 2: The genuine Aqua Pure doesn't reduce TDS either, so it appears that fridge filters are a waste of money even when they're not falsely promoted.

Input: A little over 2 1/2 years ago, I purchased a brand new front loading Whirlpool washing machine (Whirlpool LHW0050PQ) with stacking dryer. About a month ago, it stopped working (the warranty for the machine was 1 year, so it is no longer covered). The power would come on - but the machine would no longer begin wash cycles (the Start button did nothing). I had a repair person in who took several visits to diagnose the problem. In the end, it was determined that the machine required a new control panel. The control panel cost over $500. With labour, I have spent approximately $800 now. When the part was replaced, as soon as the repair person left, I did a load of laundry, only to discover that the problem still existed *exactly* as it had before. I called the repair company - who wanted to take the machine to their shop to diagnose it. What they found was that the new part had almost instantly shorted out as soon as the machine was used for the first time after replacing it. They contacted Whirlpool technical support who told them that something in the machine must be causing the short. According to the person at the repair shop that I spoke to, Whirlpool offered to give them a door latching mechanism for free for the washing machine so that they could perhaps see if it was causing the short (my repair people did install this part). In addition, Whirlpool gave me a new control panel (a new $500 part to replace the one that I bought that had burnt out - because it was still under warranty as a new part purchase). I now have the washing machine back and it seems to be working, but I have no faith whatsoever that it will continue to work for any length of time.

Here are my concerns:
- obviously, it positively sickens me that I would have to spend $800 to repair a washing machine that is only 2 1/2 years old. The washing machine was not cheap. I thought I was buying quality. This obviously wasn't the case.
- upon learning that the replacement part would cost so much, I would have just bought a new washing machine (not from Whirlpool!). However, the repair shop explained to me that my stackable Whirlpool dryer was only going to fit on top of a Whirlpool washing machine. So, to replace the washing machine would mean that I would also have to sell my dryer. Weighing the pros and cons of the situation, I decided to fix the washing machine even though it positively sickened me to give Whirlpool another cent. I find it equally repulsive that, when one buys a stackable unit, they're basically stuck if one part of it fails (this would be more acceptable, of course, if the machines lasted considerably longer than 2 1/2 years).
- when the repair person first brought the replacement part to my house, he mentioned that the replacement part was now being sold as part of a kit (control board with motor board - that's how they had purchased it from Whirlpool). He mentioned that, when parts come in a kit, it usually means the company has had problems with the part (so they sell the parts in a way that makes the many repair jobs easier). If Whirlpool has been having problems with this part, I have to wonder why they wouldn't instead compensate customers who'd bought the part in the first place. The fact that the replacement part had *exactly* the same problems as the original part makes me wonder the exact same thing.
- I have to wonder how much Whirlpool is making off of these replacement parts. It is absurd to me that any washing machine part should cost $500 - unless, of course, the company selling the part is marking up its value considerably. I really have to wonder if this isn't part of the company's business model: selling units that fail shortly after the warranty expires and then selling the parts required to fix the units at a jacked up price.
- related to the above point, the $500 replacement part has a guarantee of 3 months. Three months for something that cost over $500! In other words, if the part goes again in 4 months (and the machine's history tells me that this is a great possibility), I am completely out of luck again. I have never - ever - spent $500 on something that didn't come with a guarantee that wasn't at least a year long. You can buy a $30 toaster anywhere and it comes with at least a 1 year warranty! But I guess, considering what I believe to be their business model (see above), I'm not really that surprised by this.
- I am extremely confused by Whirlpool technical support's involvement in this. You would think that the nature of their involvement was an admission that something in the machine had caused the $500 part to go in the first place. This is especially suspect since they offered another part for free to try to make that determination. I just have to wonder why I should have had to pay $800 to replace a part that was caused by a fault with the machine in the first place.
- I have spent $800 and been without a working washing machine for over a month now. That alone is ridiculous. But, to add potential injury to insult, I now have a washing machine with parts that have proven to short out because of a deficiency with the machine. In other words, I now have to wonder if my washing machine is going to catch fire every time I use it!

I have written to Whirlpool 3 times now about this situation. All they really told me in return was that they appreciate my business and that they have added my concerns to their database. I don't think I need to explain to anyone what little consolation that has given me...

Input: This was ordered via Amazon Prime from "PrimeCo Supply" and fulfilled by Amazon. I specifically ordered this version because it was advertised as the OEM part. I was fairly confident I would get the correct part because the vendor had 100% feedback and the listing stated to report to Amazon if an aftermarket part was received.

When i opened the part, I immediately knew it was not the original LG part. It came in a plain box with a printed bar code taped on and the pump assembly had no markings for motor rating, etc. However, my washer had already been down a few days and laundry piles up fast with three kids, so I decided I would install it anyway.

After disassembling the washer and removing the old pump, i tried to put the new pump in the plastic housing, but it would not fit right. The pump looked similar, but was not the same size and the slots to slide into the housing were not in the right spot. You can see the attached picture of the difference. I could have forced it in the housing and probably made it work, but this was clearly not a very good copy of the part, so decided to just return it and get a replacement.

I ordered another one, this time directly from Amazon for a few dollars more and it was clearly the correct part. It had LG printed on the box with a part number sticker the correct printing on the unit. It fit perfectly and the washer now works great.

For future customers, the second picture shows what the box should look like. If not, you probably received some cheap knock-off like i did.

Input: I live solo in a studio with stone floors and no washer/dryer hookups. This little washer is awesome! I still go tp the laundromat for big items like comforters, etc. But for regular weekly washing for me and any friends staying over, it is perfect. One load fits about a week's worth of undies, socks, a few outfits, and maybe a towel and a pillow case. And the spin dryer works great to get the excess water out - I hang dry my clothes on a folding rack indoors and they are dry overnight usually. If I set out on a sunny day it's dry in an hour or two.

One thing that took some getting used to versus a big automatic clothes washer is that you have to be conscious and aware for the water fill up process - otherwise it will overflow and pour out. This happened once when I was not paying attention while on the phone. So be sure to set a timer! Mine fills in 5 minutes from my kitchen sink.

The other thing to get used to is multiple cycles. I work outdoors so my clothes get really dirty, so I do two cycles with soap, and two to three cycles to rinse until the water is close to completely clear. So it's a relatively involved process compared to an automatic washer. But the results are comparable, and no need to install washer/dryer hookups!

I highly recommend using this machine at a sink with a non-carpeted, sealed or stone floor below it - maybe I'm just a messy user, but seems like I always get some water on the floor when I do laundry with it.

Input: We have 24 foot of solid dryer vent pipe ending in 3 right-angles before going through the floor into the flexible dryer-vent hose coming from the dryer.  I can't get behind the dryer without moving both the washer and dryer and they are HEAVY.  So being lazy I decided to clean the vent from the outside of the house inward.  I didn't use a vacuum cleaner or a blower or suction of any kind.  I did tighten each section of tubing with pliers and taped them.  I threaded all 24 foot of tubing with the brush on the end into the outside vent and then backed it out.  I got a good amount of lint clods out.  Then I turned on the dryer to blow everything out.  I got no air coming out at all.  My fear had come true, I had forced gobs of lint into the right-angles at the end of the run.  I still didn't want to move that washer and dryer so I figured I'd try one other thing, use the clodbuster attachment.  Now I'm really getting lazy so I tightened each tubing section by hand (no pliers) and didn't use tape.  I pushed all 24 foot of tubing into the vent until I hit some resistance and then turned the tubing by hand (too lazy to hook the drill up).  Then I pulled it all out and there wasn't any lint at all that came out. So now I'm resigned to having to move the washer and dryer, but before I do I figured I might as well turn the dryer on and see what happens.  Lots of lint clods blew out and kept coming out for about 20 seconds.  I've attached pictures of it.  I'm really happy with this product and if it worked for me with all the shortcuts I took it will probably work great for you.  As a point of reference we built this house five years ago and this is the first time I ever cleaned the vent.  A load of ten bath towels used to take 45 minutes to dry, lately it's been taking 3 to 4 hours, so I knew I couldn't put cleaning the pipe off any longer.

Input: From the reviews I watched, it looked like a great product. I ended up caving to my curiosity and purchasing the Wonderwash.

First impressions, the base is extremely flismy / flexible. I wish they made it with higher quality plastics. I am not sure if it will be prone to cracking / snapping in the future, but the flexing is annoying if only because the tank wobbles while spinning.

Unfortunately, once I filled it up with water, the bottom started leaking. Given that it "has a patented pressure system that forces detergent into the fabric at high speed for a fast, efficient, economic and very easy wash", if it leaks, it means the pressure isn't being maintained.  I ignored it and proceeded to do a trial wash. The only complain I have then is that it is wobbly. Water was being flung into my face due to the leak, but I am assuming that it is a defect and it does not normally leak (and thus, water will not be flung into your face).

If what I received wasn't defective, I would likely give this 4 stars - pending durability assessments.

I will be contacting Laundry Alternative to see what can be done, and I will update this review accordingly.

Update 1:

Received a replacement tub. I haven't gotten a chance to do a wash yet, but I did fill it with some water to check for leaks - no leaks yet, yay!

Update 2:

The tub seems to work fine now. Did a load of wash and worked out as intended. My only concern is that the metal (the rod that holds the handle) will eventually corrode due to friction and exposure to water.

I also have another quality issue. The metal rings (in the base - used to support the actual tub) are flaking. I noticed little gray flakes scattered on the surface I was using to do the washing. Upon closer inspection, it was coming off the metal rings. Only time can tell what issues this will cause in the future.

I am fairly in between whether or not I would recommend this product. Quality is up in the air, but it definitely works as long as it holds up. If you live in an apartment and pay per load in the basement/in the laundromat, this will pay itself off in about 30 loads. Question is, would it last 30 loads (30 loads in laundromat terms is really like 60-80 wonderwash terms due to difference in size).

Input: This is a small lightweight washer alternative, unfortunately..while yes, it sort of manages to wash clothes...it's not all that effective. You can essentially accomplish the same level of clean by swirling your clothes in a bucket for 5 mins. Which, would be cheaper than this system. The clothes don't come out that clean(as I said, it's the same as swirling clothes in a bucket) and in fact you get cleaner clothes by washing the clothes by hand. In fact, I think I prefer the level of cleanliness from hand washing than I do from this washer.

The unit it's self is fairly sturdy, but the clips used to hold the system on it's "Stand" come out rather easily which can be annoying. especially if you are using the washer in sink or tub, and the clip goes down the drain.

The hole for your clothes also is fairly small. Not too much of an issue for light clothes, but stiff clothing like jeans are a bit tough to get in and out..and even when you get the clothes out? There's a good chance water will be everywhere! So make sure you use this outside, or in a sink or tub..some place where having water pool out everywhere isn't an issue.

Another thing that irked me, was the thing didn't include any kind of assembly manual. Sure, it's not too difficult to figure out how it's put together, but it still would be handy to have that little bit of help along the way.

All in all, I wouldn't really recommend this to anyone, since there are better washing machine alternatives out there (Including hand washing) but it does SLIGHTLY work, so it doesn't get a completely failing mark in my book....I may still use it on occasion, but most likely I will stick with hand washing.

Input: Poor calibration:
Even when the remote sensor is sitting right next to the base station, the indoor and outdoor temperatures are off by a degree or two.

Uninspired support:
I called support to ask if I could recalibrate. I was 17th in line. After five minutes or so, I'd only gotten down to #10 in line, so I opted to have them call me back. "without losing my place in line!"  They didn't call back. Approx 2 hours later, I remembered, and called them again. They'd already closed. (Support til 5pm Central) No option to leave a message. Lame. ...To their credit, they did eventually call back that same day. Support was friendly but not helpful.

Poor documentation:
Support told me that my degree or so of discrepancy was within the +/-2 degree calibration present in "all thermometers".
Neither the manual nor product listing mentions this. I call BS, anyhow. There are plenty of more diligently calibrated thermometers out there.

Poor readability:
If the lighting is not perfect, it's difficult to read both temperatures from some angles when only a few feet away.
I would not purchase this item again. I use one other AcuRite item and while it's nothing to write home about, it's okay, so I'm not totally severing consumer/company ties ;)

...But, after living with it for a few months, I added a couple more stars. Why? I got over the fact that it's poorly calibrated. I don't even remember which one is colder/hotter than the other. I've just resolved to be okay knowing I'm somewhere in the ballpark when I look at the AcuRite 00611A3.

Input: I've been in IT, and a high-tech management consultant, for pushing 40 years.  I've installed almost literally every non-mainframe computer printer -- and at least one printer from literally every brand, family and/or generation of non-mainframe printers (and, don't get me wrong, I've installed no small number of mainframe printers, too) -- ever made.  No, really... I'm that both old and experienced. I've really paid my dues, and I really know what I'm talking about...

...and so if you'll just bother to really read and understand what I'm here writing (and that to which I link), you'll learn why this printer's good, and why you should buy it, as well as how to get the biggest bang for your buck from it.

This really is a first-rate printer, have no doubts about that. However, there are things the user needs to know in order to fully leverage it to its greatest advantage and benefit. If one buys this printer and expects it to behave like an HP (or even an Epson), for example, then one will be disappointed. Most of the negative reviews, here, are from people who thought it would all be just plug-and-play, and who weren't willing to figure it all out (or, more accurately, to just bother to read the various documentation, and watch a video or two); and so they come here and embarrass themselves with ridiculous comments. In what I'm here writing, I refer you to my comment beneath Canon's official Pixma MX922 video, over on Youtube: be sure, if you go there, to read the even *MORE* ridiculous comments by the, I'm sorry, idiots who so embarrass themselves with their ignorance and its revelation of their having not bothered to pick-up and read the printer's excellent documentation.

One must learn the nuances of this device; must set it up properly and then properly configure both it and the "printers" area of one's copy of Windows or iOS; and then one must know a little something about inks and the best ways to both buy and use them.  Fail to read the manual, or try to set-up the device without using the "Quick Start" guide (and follow it, exactly); or fail to download and use the most-up-to-date software from the Canon site; or fail to ensure that the printer's using the most current firmware -- all of that sort of thing -- and it will, I can virtually guarantee, disappoint you.

It's not that this printer is "high maintenance": it is not. And it's not that this printer is persnickety, or sensitive, or fragile or anything like that: it is none of those things.  But it's a classic Canon product, which means, to we who've been installing them for many years, that the manufacturer bothers to provide all the information that the user could possibly need to know in order to properly use and enjoy the product via videos, manuals, bulletins, help files, etc...

...but if the user won't bother to read about and truly learn it, then said user gets exactly what s/he deserves.  Simple as that.

For a lousy hundred bucks (or, more accurately these days, for even less) this is, hands down, one of the best little printers you could buy... especially if you take halfway-serious photographs in life, and want to be able to print them out really nicely.  For me, the fact that I can print directly onto CDs and DVDs is yet another reason why I finally decided to buy one of these.  Yes, I still have my much higher-end HP printer for serious (and seriously-fast) office-style mostly-just-text printing; and the truth is that that HP can print a little bit sharper and better quality text -- especially by comparison when in draft mode; and also using a tiny bit less ink -- than can this Canon...

...but, all that notwithstanding, I'm now using this MX922 as my basic personal printer, scanner, fax machine; and, especially, as my photo printer and that which I use for CD/DVD labeling (because I no longer have to buy labels; I can print directly onto CDs and DVDs which are made to be printed on) instead of the HP, now.  It's a plenty-fast scanner/copier; it faxes well; and for 99% of the text documents that I could ever need to print, it's perfectly clear and sharp and fine. Only if I had to print super-high-quality text, on super-high-quality bond paper, at fairly high speed, might I switch-over to the HP...

...but, that said, honestly, I've learned that the paper one uses has almost more to do with that than anything else.  The Canon ink is different from HP inks; sadly, Canon inks tend to bleed into cotton bond papers more than HP inks; and so it gives the impression to the inexperienced user that HP printers print more sharp text than do Canon printers.  But if you just make sure the paper on which you're printing is "hard" enough, and has a lower fiber content, then even the Canon printer, when doing super-high quality printing, is razor sharp. So don't be fooled by those who insist that HP printers are always sharper. They *can* be, but they're not always: it depends, in large measure, on the paper used.

At any rate, this printer, once everything is just right (and that's the operative phrase, here), is really nice. No, really. I love it. Is it my favorite device of its type, ever?  Of COURSE not... but then, again, I'm old; and I've seen, in my life, some of the best equipment ever made by any manufacturer, anywhere.  But this little device -- once it's properly set-up and everything's configured right, and everything's tested and works; and once you've got the latest firmware, and the latest printer software and utilities (and it, too, is properly configured), and ONCE YOU BOTHER TO REALLY-AND-TRULY LEARN HOW TO USE IT ALL -- is really quite nice.  Be careful believing the negative reviews, here: this device -- like most Canon products -- requires no small investment on the part of the user to first get things just right, and to then actually learn how to use it.  Fail to make that investment, and you'll be unhappy.

Beneath the official Canon Pixma MX922 video, over on YouTube, I wrote a long comment which is probably the best and most useful thing that anyone either owning or considering owning this device could ever read. Though it covers several areas, it mostly covers inks... the single highest ongoing cost of owning any printer; and Canon printers, unlike HP printers (though very similar to Epson printers), tend to use a lot of ink, and to "pile on" ink, in order to achieve even only black colors.  Remember that with ink, unlike with light, the presence of all colors makes black; whereas with light, the presence of all colors makes white.  Canon leverages that to create excellent blacks and dazzling shades of both gray and all colors...

...but, boy-oh-boy, does Canon ever use a lot of ink.  Fortunately, there are ways to configure both the printer and the "printers" area of one's copy of Windows or iOS to default everything to "draft" mode, using only black ink, for everyday printing; and then if you want high-quality mode, then all you have to do is go into printer settings, just before sending a job to the printer, right on your computer screen, and set everything, just for that print job, to high-quality using all colors of ink.  Just doing that will save you a ton of money on ink in the long run...

...and then, beyond that, if you're willing to consider the admittedly risky business of purchasing aftermarket inks and refillable ink cartridges, then you can lower your ink costs by quite literally a factor of around 8... or even more.  But don't underestimate my use of the word "risky" in that immediately-previous sentence: In my comment over on YouTube to which I herein earlier refer (and to which I'll link you in a moment), I cover exactly why some -- not all, mind you, but at least some; maybe even most -- aftermarket inks are a really bad idea. If they're not made to the same high-quality standards as Canon inks, then they will clog-up the print-head nozzles in this printer, but fast; and once that happens, you're done, because print heads for all ink jet printers, regardless of brand, tend to be very expensive... so expensive that by the time you replace the print heads, you've probably paid for most of a whole new printer.  An example: a typical HP OfficeJet-Pro printer might cost two- to three-hundred bucks; and a pair of print heads for most of them will run maybe $60 to $90 per head, for a total of $120 to $180 for the pair. At that point, once you factor-in all the other wear-and-tear variables, it can start to make more sense to just buy a whole new printer, believe it or not.

Printer manufacturers, you must understand, are not really in the business, anymore, of selling the printers, themselves. Rather, it's all that expensive ink, over the life of the printer, in which they're so interested in selling you. Consequently, most printer manufacturers now practically give away their printers; and so that's why a pair of print heads for most printers costs almost as much as an entirely new printer. It's also why most printers, anymore, aren't really repairable. They're so cheap, now, that it's almost as inexpensive to just replace them as it is to repair them, or to purchase new print heads for them.  Even replacing the little illuminating light tube used by the scanner, on most of these printers, today, is cost-prohibitive; and can cost nearly as much as just replacing the whole printer. It's kinda' silly, if you think about it; but it's just the things are, today.

At any rate, make sure your eyes are wide open about using aftermarket inks.  I use them, but then, again, I know how to determine if they're really high quality; and I know where and how to buy them.  And so my (as well as my clients'... at least if they listen to me) printers still last, without damage to their print heads from aftermarket inks. However, if you cannot ensure that you, too, can get the really good aftermarket inks, then, trust me, you'll  end-up regretting using them.  That said, if you can, then... well... all I can say is: WOW!  What a savings!  Where Canon-branded inks, almost no matter how you buy them, cost from maybe 3 to 5 cents per page, give or take, a good set of aftermarket high-capacity refillable ink cartridges (with the auto-reset chips in them), along with the syringe-type thingies used to inject ink into said cartridges, plus if you buy your both pigment and dye ink in big 17- to 20-oz bottles made especially for the Canon Pixma MX-series, it can lower your per-page cost to just a fraction of a penny... in fact, seriously, it can be a fraction of a fraction per page.  I kid you not: the savings from aftermarket inks can be quite stunning!

In fact, the aftermarket ink savings can be *SO* unbelievable that even if you purchase cheap inks which end-up shortening the life of the printer, the cost of the printer is so low, anymore, that it can almost still be cheaper to use even the crappy aftermarket inks; and then when they finally kill the printer (and, trust me, they will), just buy a whole new printer and do it all over again.  Seriously: do the math, and you'll see.

Anyway, it's now time to tell you how to go read that long comment of mine beneath the official Canon Pixma MX-922 video over on YouTube from which you'll learn so much... especially about ink cartridges.  I'll go ahead and link to it, here, but Amazon censors are fairly notorious for deleting such links (even though, in this case, it will just help Amazon to sell the MX922 printer, here) and so I humbly request that the following link be allowed.

SEE | http://youtu.be/JJJRDkSlzww  (mine is the "LINKED COMMENT" there)

If Amazon censors it, then you may also type EXACTLY this (quotation marks and all) into the Google search page box...

"Canon PIXMA Printer: PIXMA MX922" "Gregg DesElms"

...and it should be the second (after the ad, if there is one) search result (or if you use an ad-blocker, then maybe it'll be the first -- and possibly only, after all duplicates have been removed -- search result).  Once you're on the YouTube page, then just scroll down to (or search for) my name "Gregg DesElms" to find my comment with the words "THE ONE COMMENT, HERE, THAT EVERYONE SHOULD READ!" at the very top.  Then click on the "Read more (369 lines)" link to expand it.  Yes, it's long, but it's so worth it that I promise you won't mind.

If you can't find it, let me know in a comment, here, after which maybe I'll just copy-and-paste it into a comment to this review or something.  One way or another I'll somehow make sure you can all read it, by hook or by crook.

And... oh, yeah... two more things...

First, some here (and elsewhere) complain that this printer is slow; that the first copy of anything printed or scanned/copied takes a long time to come out of the printer because of some kind of initialization or warm-up necessary because the printer sort of "sleeps" if not used for a while.  Well, the printer can be configured so that it never sleeps; and, believe me, so doing doesn't use a lot of electricity or suddenly make the printer ecologically unsound.  In fact, I think some of the newest models, with the newest firmware (which can be downloaded and installed into the older models), default to not sleeping because of those complaints early in this model's life. So don't worry about that one: it's configurable.

Second, as with all printers of this printer's type, this one needs to be used.  If you tend to never print, such that the printer just sits there, for days upon days, never printing anything, then it will eventually fail in various ways -- including and especially, getting clogged-up print head nozzles -- just when you really need it. Yes, it'll technically be a waste of both ink and paper, but try to run a little something through the printer every day, if possible.  Just three to five pages per day, of something -- anything -- will help keep it in decent condition.  High-capacity, high-speed HP printers are even worse about that than are Canons: if you don't use those HPs every day, then, wow!, they really go bad fast. Epsons, too, but not quite as much.  Canons are a little bit better about it, but you still need to use them a little... if not every single day, then at least three or four times per week. Print or copy something every now and then just to keep the MX922 printer in decent shape, ready for use whenever you need it.  And if you default the printer to draft mode and using just black ink (as I herein earlier recommended), then go out of your way to print at least a page or two, every now and then (once or twice weekly, I recommend), in full -- maybe even high-quality (which, yes, uses a lot of ink) -- color, just to keep the color inkjet nozzles clear and working well, too.

Hope that helps!

_________________________
Gregg L. DesElms
Napa, California USA

Input: This printer has been great so far. I was a little leary at first, because I had a negative experience with low-cost color laser printer in the past, and because several users were getting very dark prints.

Set-up was a breeze, and I had no problems printing right away.
Don't bother with the CD. Just download the latest driver right off the HP website.

I too, found my initial prints way too dark. (Mac OS X 10.7, Adobe Illustrator CS5)
After some fiddling with the settings, and a lot of trial and error, I am now getting almost perfect results. Here's what I did:

Connect to the printer's IP address using a browser.
In the System tab, go to Print Density:
Leave everything at 0, except for the Midtones. Make all the Midtones at -4.

In the "Printer..." options contained in the Print panel:
ColorMatching: ColorSync: Automatic (hp color LaserJet CYMK V402)
Color/Quality Options: HP EasyColor: ON

The color is best when I leave my Document Color Mode in RBG.

Overall, this is a great printer for the price. If it weren't for the difficulty in finding the correct color settings, I'd give it a 5 star rating. The default color densities are way way off, but fortunately you can fix this with some effort.

EDIT:
Over a year later, I finally had to change the black toner that came with the printer, and I print quite a variety of material, from simple text to full pages of color. Still running on the original color toner, although it has said it's been empty for at least 6 months. Don't listen to it. Eventually you may notice that the color starts to change slightly as the toner gets lower, but it's still plenty usable.

This printer has turned out to be an excellent purchase.

Input: Updated 2/4/18--  Good phone--  except I had a problem with programming the memory--  I noticed that I could successfully program a 7-digit local number, but attempts to enter memory with an 11-digit long-distance number were unsuccessful.  Other than that--  great phone... loud/clear sound, pleasant ringer, and LOW cost.  This would be a five-star if it weren't for the memory problem with 11-digits.

The difficulty in adding a long number into memory is apparently due to my local telephone exchange interrupting with a recorded message: "If you would like to make a call....".  This happens because they sensed the phone was "off the hook" with no dialing while attempting to add to the memory.  This interruption causes the intended number to not be put into memory correctly.  No problem with a local 7-digit number because you have enough time before the interruption.  The solution--  place the numbers into memory as fast as you can doing the seven
steps required, and repeat until you have done it without getting the interruption (the time varies--  15 or 20 seconds).

Input: This is a great mouse pad.  I purchased 1 for my office and one for my home.  They do what they are supposed to do and are comfortable on my wrists.  It is well made and the company shipped fast and genuinely cares about the products and customers.
If you are looking for a anice mousepad with ergonomic support you can't go wrong here.

There is one negative I noticed about both mouse pads and I removed a star because of it.  They have a really strong smell that has lasted several weeks.  It off gasses for a long time.  At first it was really strong.  I purchased this and it was delivered on 1/22/16.  I was prompted to write this review when I got to work today 2/9/16 as I still smell the mouse pad.  It is not nearly as strong, but the smell is definitely there on both mouse pads.  I am not super sensitive to smells in any way so this caught me by surprise.  Overall this is a nice mouse pad but the smell could be an issue if you have sensitivity to smell or would be bothered by the smell.

6. **Shipping Speed**: Attribute Description - The speed of delivery. Attribute Value - Fast (the product was shipped quickly)
7. **Smell Intensity**: Attribute Description - The strength of the product's smell. Attribute Value - Strong (the smell is "really strong" and "lasts several weeks")
8. **Smell Persistence**: Attribute Description - How long the product's smell lasts. Attribute Value - Long-lasting (the smell is still present after several weeks)
9. **Sensitivity to Smell**: Attribute Description - The reviewer's sensitivity to smells. Attribute Value - Low (the reviewer is "not super sensitive to smells")
10. **Recommendation**: Attribute Description - Whether the reviewer recommends the product. Attribute Value - Conditional (recommended, but with a warning about the smell)
11. **Emotional Tone**: Attribute Description - The emotional tone of the review. Attribute Value - Generally Positive, with a hint of Frustration (due to the smell issue)
12. **Objectivity**: Attribute Description - The reviewer's level of objectivity. Attribute Value - High (the reviewer provides both positive and negative comments)
13. **Helpfulness**: Attribute Description - The reviewer's intention to help others. Attribute Value - High (the reviewer provides detailed feedback to inform others)

Input: The PIXMA MG5720 is a wireless print/scan/copy device with outstanding output quality. A lot of thought went into making it easy to set up and use, although we managed to defeat some of that in the early going. I really liked the way it presented out of the box with the instruction sheets on top. They are actually easy to follow, so most people will have the physical setup done very quickly. The ink tanks load into their rack very positively: it would be very hard to get it wrong.

Getting wireless connectivity and cloud functions set up requires getting to the settings menu, which requires actually noticing that the front panel display scrolls up and down (circularly), with a press of the up and down buttons. I did not, however, catch on to that until my kid asked if there was more to print because the display said "1/3."

LAN and Cloud setup are straightforward after that. The aforementioned instruction sheets have flowcharts so that you are told exactly what to do to set up the device on wireless only, or also have a USB connection to a computer.

It's very satisfying to be able to save something on your phone and send it to Google Cloud Print, or even just share something from an app. Futuristic!

The other caution you must observe when printing letter size pages is to pull out the center tab on the paper catcher; if you don't, it will look like cats got your output. This is, however, pretty normal for this kind of printer.

Canon has a Creative Park website with a number of templates for greeting cards, scrapbook pages, calendars, you name it. Some is premium, but a lot is free, and it's quick to use.

One of my favorite features is two-sided printing,. I do a lot of handouts and mini-reports that just look a ton more professional when printed on both sides. I also experienced a moment of techno-rapture watching it suck the paper back in to print the second side for the first time.

I'm knocking off one star, though, for the fact that the printer is ungraceful about printing (at least from a PC) when it's turned off. I should be able to just go turn it on and have it start printing, but instead I have to click this and poke that. It doesn't always weather Wi-fi glitches well, either, but so far that has only required entering and leaving setup. Still, more time wasted at the keyboard or the control panel that could have been productive.

I'm waiting to see what my ink budget needs to be. It's very nice that ink tank levels are available right on the device, so you won't be caught by surprise. Also, the black tank is the largest, which was clever.

Overall, it's a great device. Glad to have it in my "SOHO" environment (aka the desk in the dining room).

3. **User Experience**: Attribute Description - The reviewer's overall experience with the device. Attribute Value - Satisfying
4. **Frustration Level**: Attribute Description - The level of frustration experienced by the reviewer. Attribute Value - Low (with some minor annoyances)
5. **Excitement**: Attribute Description - The level of enthusiasm or excitement expressed by the reviewer. Attribute Value - High (e.g., "Futuristic!", "techno-rapture")

9. **Design Appreciation**: Attribute Description - The reviewer's appreciation for the device's design. Attribute Value - High (e.g., "clever" design of ink tanks)

Input: I admit to having seen the positive and negative reviews of this product before purchasing it recently.  I may return it - we'll see.

So far, in my limited one-weeks' analysis of this item (and from a non-technical person), I will first mention the things about it that bug me.

1.) Using the stylus.  You end up having to go back and forth trying to handprint the darn letter.  The screen is not sensitive enough (or is too sensitive and perhaps there's another adjustment I can make in preferences that I have not yet tried).  It annoys me that I have to fix "typos" because the screen thought I wrote and "l" and a "c" when I wrote a "k", for example.  There's a handful of letters that this happens with.

2.) The option of using the "keypad" is there, but have you tried to see that keyboard and actually "type" with the stylus?  If you have and love it, you have better eyesight than I do.  The font is TINY to me.  (Though I admit, I need reading glasses.)

3.) There really does exist a high-pitch sound when the unit is on.  I would not have noticed it, though, if someone here didn't mention it.  It's surely there.

4.) I live in fear of the screen smashing by dropping it, since the insurance is just plain stupid to carry on a system that was only $200.00.

Anyway, the good points so far:

1.) I've had no trouble syncing my data to Outlook.
2.) Having the "tasks" features, the calendar, and even the calculator is nice.  There's still much more to be discovered, as mentioned, I've had it only a week.
3.) Seems nice to not have paperwork (bits of paper all around with notes on it).  I even keep my grocery list items in it...I jot them in when I run out of something.  I plan to sync it up and print it from Outlook for this weekend shop.

I still am on the fence if this was the right system for me.  My sister keeps telling me it seems to be more of an aggravation in some ways (having to back it up daily and charge it daily, etc, and that the font is too small, and then theres the issues with the stylus whereby it's just not doing it's job all the time. Oh, and the delay of WHEN you type in the letter to when it actually appears on your screen can be like watching paint dry.

Having said ALL that, maybe if I get my eyes checked, I'd just get used to the small font and avoid the stylus OR double check that I've got Mr Pointy properly set up.

Input: I am still fooling around with this combo printer/scanner/copier.  First impressions:

Setup was easy, wi-fi connectivity works pretty well for me on my desktop (I have macs) but the laptop seems to have an issue with finding the printer in the preferences.  It prints fairly well.  The first inks that came with printer lasted a long time.  If you get a sign that says "low ink", keep using it until it forces you to change - the inks will last a long time.  The copier works okay, although the buttons on this printer are confusing (no "copy" in English, just symbols - annoying).  I had to put labels next to the icons to remind me of which is copy, etc.  The screen is fairly easy to read.  Speaking of copying, the glass is long, and if you put down a 8.5 X 11 document to copy, and put it at the intuitively correct end, it cuts off the document.  So you have to place it opposite of where you think it should go.  (same with scan position, described below). poor design in that regard.

I am extremely disappointed in the scanner part of this printer. The Epson scanning software is pretty bad.  You cannot edit a document (crop, rotate, etc) before you scan it.....(?). It insists on putting a number 1 after whatever you title the resulting document.  Canon's scanner software is far superior in this regard.  Plus, to scan a document, you put the document down on the plate in the position that it would be to copy straight up, but it's upside down in the scan.... ?  Don't know who thought that up!  And remember, you can't pre-edit it before the scan.  Annoying. It's super complicated to do anything than just scan one page.  Scanning multiple pages in one PDF document takes forever - because you have to keep "adding" a page and previewing it) - it all takes a lot of time.

You also have to set up the scan settings to recognize the wifi before you can use the scanner part.  I had to have Epson walk me through this (they were very nice and helpful).  but the software itself gets a D grade for its lack of editing features pre-scan and unnecessary complications scanning a multiple page document.  I haven't tried scanning photographs yet, so don't know if you can put down 4 photos on the glass and have the scanner distinguish that they're 4 separate images (has anyone done that yet?)
