Input: Pros: (1) some funny one-liners, (2) inexpensive, (3) light-weight

Cons: (1) based on two stereotypes that some may have difficult to relate to in the 21st century: (i) woman are confined to the domestic quarters, (ii) men are meatheads, and thus, (2) funny one-liners few and far between

I bought this book for my girlfriend for some comedic light-reading, but we both have difficulty finding it funny (it has a few lines that led to laughter).  I think the problem is that my girlfriend and I are both independent professionals, and cannot relate to this book overall.  For example, I don't spend my time blowing my weekly paycheck at the horse track or betting on the Giants, just as my girlfriend doesn't spend her time scrubbing toilets and preparing dinner whilst adorned with an apron and hair scarf.  Frankly speaking, I don't understand why anyone would want to be with a compulsive gambler, or how a relationship could be based on the division of labor dictated by antiquated gender roles rather than mutual respect and pragmatism (e.g., if one partner is a more efficient cook, then that partner should probably play a larger role in cooking, regardless of the partner's gender).  But that is just me, and others can live the way they want within the boundaries of the law defined by our state and federal legislatures.

If you (a man) are a compulsive gambler/alcoholic, lacking any modicum of self-control and financial savvy, and are dating/married to another (a woman) who often has to talk you out of joining in on cockamamie schemes that can quite possibly lead to both physical and financial ruin, or the opposite, then you can probably relate to this book more and find it funny overall.  If not save, the $10 bucks.

Input: I received a free Adobe Digital Editions copy of this book from the publisher through Netgalley, this has not compromised my ability to write an honest and critical review of the book.

28/1 - 1.5 to 2 stars (2 stars for GR because it wasn't completely full of grammatical, punctuational and spelling errors).  While it wasn't full of errors they weren't completely absent.  This sentence is a perfect example: "It has always rankled me that what is best for the gentleman is not always best for the lady yet society seems bent on keeping it these inconvenient methods."  Missing comma and what does "bent on keeping it these inconvenient methods." mean?  Obviously,  Portman is trying to convey something along the lines of 'what's good for the goose should be good for the gander', but those last seven words make absolutely no sense (especially 'inconvenient' as it has nothing to do with the gender differences in those days in this context).

The opening lines state "I am with child, again.  In the unfortunate event I do not recover from this birth, I write my confessions in this diary."  Reading those lines I assumed that Cecelia had experienced previous difficult pregnancies, been warned not to become pregnant again or was in such an abusive relationship that she feared for her life.  But, other than some bad morning sickness with each pregnancy (the possibly deadly pregnancy she's talking about will be her fifth successful birth of five pregnancies - she hasn't lost any children through miscarriage), she suffered no more than any other pregnant woman of the day would have been expected to.  Other than this opening paragraph her fears for her life aren't mentioned again - if she had actually had reasons to fear for her life that might have made the book more interesting.

Cecelia says she's writing this 'diary/confessional' to distract herself from her growing (unfounded) fear and because she wants to explain to 'those she loves' the reasons for the rumours surrounding her marriage to William.  If she's writing to her family members why does she feel the need to 'state that her husband was known to be something of a rake'?  Wouldn't they already know all about his reputation?  To be continued after dinner...

After dinner - Now to the erotica genre this has been placed into.  What the hell?  How can anyone call the sex scenes in this book erotic?  The sex is peppered with sentences like this catastrophe: "Without warning his hand came around and gripped my buttock, he squeezed it hard and the pain flashed through my entire body.  I gasped out aloud.  Despite the grinding weight and heaviness in my womb, a sure indicator of my body's interest in him, I was growing increasingly fearful.
'To the bed with you, good woman,' William cried with gregarious chivalry."I know this because Cecelia herself states earlier that her marriage was arranged very shortly after the start of her first season.  How is "To bed with you, good woman," chivalrous?  I would be more inclined to say it's imperious and domineering.

I think I could safely diagnose Portman with acyrologia (from afar, even), specifically cacozelia - a kind of acyrologia in which one uses newfangled speech or Latinate diction in order to appear learned.  I think learning of this condition is going to be unbelievably useful in writing reviews of this kind - you know, where the book is bad.  I would not recommend this to anyone looking for good erotica, or even erotica at all as not one line of this is erotic.

Input: The idea behind this book is quite compelling - build up a bar using a minimal number of bottles required for an increasingly complex array of cocktails.

However, the authors fudge on the 12-bottle rule by having you make your own syrups, infusions, and mixers. (Homemade orgeat syrup? No. Just buy a bottle of amaretto)

They also exclude beer, wine, and cider from the count, even when a drink such as a French 75 must include sparkling wine.

Beyond this, they borrow heavily from other, better books such as The Drunken Botanist by Amy Stewart, and fail to properly include a bibliography.

Also, no tequila! Thus, it fails the basic test of being a reference/recipe book.

Much of the above could be forgiven if it ended up just being a large collection of drink recipies interspersed with colorful anecdotes, but the book fails utterly at being a recipe book, because of the physical printing of the book.

The dense, paperback, glue-spine format means the book absolutely will never lay open unless you break the spine at every recipe you wish to make, and if you do this, the pages begin to fall out.

Finally, very little attention is paid to technique, a far better way of learning good mixology. One would be far better served buying Jeffrey Morgenthaler's, The Bar Book, and looking up recipes on Wikipedia.

Input: All opinions of this review are strictly my own.  My review may or may not contain some spoilers.

I'm extremely disappointed with this book. It had a really good potential to be an exciting short read. However, the author rushed through the plot so there was no wondering why it happened, who was involved, what they hoped to gain, etc.

Katya's parents are murdered and she finds out their secrets in a safety deposit box. After tracking down her uncle by getting a job as a stripper, she later learns with the help of Nik that her uncle set up mom and was behind the murder.

Now, other than the rushed information that we get, it would've been nice to actually have the parents in the story or maybe have had the book start from the mother's or even grandfather's pov and lead up to this point.

The major problem with this book is that is suddenly suddenly ends. Nik's cousin (who is the main focus of book 2 in this set) comes to help out but leaves when he says he got some possible Intel he must get in person and flies to Tampa. We never how the confirmation between Katya and her uncle go, if her uncle was behind setting up Nik (the uncle is Nik's second in command), we don't know the information Grigori received, if any, in Florida (though maybe it's in his book?), we never learn if Katya takes her place in the family. There are just too many unknowns. This book is very unfinished like the author stopped and decided to just publish what little she had.

I can't recommend this book or any of the other books. While each is a based on a different male character none of the stories are completely finished.

Input: The Confessions of Congressman X
By; Robert Atkinson

  I ordered this book before it was even printed. It came in the mail today. It is 5x8x1/4. I received a discounted cost of $8.96. The print is large on 65 pages. It took me 20 minutes to read. I believe the whole thing is a scam to suck small change from those of us who still care about our country and desperately want government reformed to provide the leadership so obviously missing today. I found nothing new except that it was stated as fact, where people like me so far removed from the process can only assume, based on the reality of the lack of progress we hope to see. We hear fine words like Reform the Income Tax while there is never any action taken in that regard.
  I can accept and believe that these were the words of a Congressman. We all know, or at least, should know that what is described is how Congress functions today and has for many years now becoming more and more disconnected with reality and what could and should be done to get us going again. The ease of buying Congress was only exaggerated by the Supreme Court ruling on Citizens United when any restrictions on the use of money were lifted. He estimates that the 2016 elections for President and Congress will exceed $10 Billion dollars.
  He is a Democrat but could just as easily have been a Republican. On a 60 Minute program a month ago Congress was exposed on fund raising. There are actually two buildings located near the Capitol dedicated to the raising of funds to support the candidates and their party. It was reported that they were duty bound to spend four hours each day calling and asking for money. I wonder if the tax payers paid for the construction of these buildings.
  The essence of the book was how easy it is to dupe the Public. Most have little knowledge of government. It is my belief that Civics, as we were taught in my day, is no longer considered important to teach the youth of today. I will claim the same for American history. Instead of holding those great men in high esteem, the children are told they were slave holders and therefore not worthy of respect. Is it any wonder therefore that they have little respect for how this great country evolved over the Centuries? That is why it was so easy to remove President Andrew Jackson from our currency and replace with a female (any female).
  Thirteen years ago when my son installed a computer for me to use, I started writing. First was my biography closely followed by what I refer to as my Angry Man books. I researched the best I could, read numerous serious books and wrote what I felt would be received as information that could be used if multiplied by those reading and sharing. There is no question I am a complete failure. The only way I could reach anyone was to give the books away to as many as I thought might be interested. Books sold are less than your finger digits. I am not even convinced that most who were given even read other than skimming.
  The nut of it is that I am not going to report on the content of this book as it would be of no use. Buy it and read for yourself if interested. You will not find anything that you should not know yourself if you are in the least interested in your country and its future.

Jack B. Walters
June 3, 2016

Input: This story has potential and makes a decent start, but somewhere along the line it feels as if Ms. Kirkpatrick panicked and rushed to get through to the end. When you have such compelling material to work with - a young girl from a broken home, mother working two jobs to keep them on the fringes of the best school system in the neighborhood, a drug dealing relative, and all the privileged, wealthy classmates - it seems to me that the book could have covered consequences and reality a bit better.

When the topic got tough it felt as though we got the dime tour rather than the full price tour. I wish there had been more time spent exploring the familial relationships and the why/how things ended up the way they did. More time was spent on trivial things than on the meat of the story. While I understand that this was written targeting the YA audience, I was disappointed to discover that it dumbed things down for them, not giving them enough credit to handle the darker, more complex side of growing up and of life in general.

Most depressing was the message that it sent, or should I say didn't send. Sure, things could have ended as they did, but odds are they also could have ended drastically differently. The ending just felt false to me, which I find depressing as it could easily influence people to make very poor decisions, believing that they'll walk away without any consequences. It plays directly into the "that will never happen to me" mindset so dominant in our society, and most especially in the younger generations. Heck, it stays with some people their entire lives, however long, or short, they may be.

I'm sorry to say that this is not a book I would recommend for the intended audience. There are simply too many mixed messages and not enough realistic consequences for actions taken.

Input: Yes, almost ALL gaffers tape is black or green screeen green nowdays, but white has some great uses in the cable and electrical department.

It makes great quick labels for cables - cut a 6" piece and wrap it around the cable then write on it with a black sharpie where it feeds from

For shipping crates or steel cornered boxes, white gaffers tape is perfect to label it - this gives you a 2" tall writing space for the contents, the next location, and what department its for (FOH, DMX, mics, etc)

Another use for repeating shows is standing marks on the stage floor that come off when you are done without scrubbing.  Put a 12" piece where you want your actors, and write on it SCENE 2, Andy's Toes go here.  Using 3 pieces you can make arrows to direct motion on the stage floor - visable to the actors, not the audience.  Some hosts have their personal space - mark it with white gaffer's tape and write guests stay behind line.  This also helps with camera placement.

I've even had costume ask to "borrow" (yea right) some to mend a dress - they were amazed it didn't show afterwards and you bet it didn't come off!  I gave them a roll to score some points.  Now if their suspenders fall down they can fix it and think of what a nice guy the sound man was.

Not all gaffer's tape is black.  If you have a few rolls of black, a roll of white, and a roll or two of green depending on your backdrops you'll do fine.  It's adhesive strength is the same no matter the color so you get the effect you are looking for that does not come off until you are wrapped up.

(Advice: Keep regular rags around for sopping up dirt, like on the porch railings...and microfiber cloths for doing a quick wipe on glass/mirrors).

There are similar steamers made by the same manufacturer (Steamfast), including SteamFast brand, McCullough, and it looks like Wagner has the same product design, and I think I came across other brands in my research. Input: Buyer beware, that's all I can say!

When I first got this robot, it cleaned amazingly well. But it seems that my initial positive first impression has only made my disappointment now even greater. After a month, it couldn't even finish the first of its three cleaning rounds without stopping and showing the message "My vision is blocked"! I have come home to an empty charging station more than once and been forced to go on a hunt around my house for the vacuum.

I tried everything from anti-static spray to a deep clean to just kicking it! And to make matters worse, the Neato Robotics Customer Service is the worst I have ever encountered! The last thing I want when trying to find a solution to a broken product is to be belittled and treated like a child by a rude service rep!! Not to mention, the "warranty" they offer is insane! I would have had to pay for shipping if I sent in my current robot- that would be from Ohio to California! With such a high price, I might as well buy a new one and throw the other away. And in return, I would only get a refurbished model (they say it's "as good as new"), and all after having to give them my credit card number! That's like returning a sweater with a stain in exchange for an older one with a patched hole in it, but having to give them my social security number first! And I've seen their responses to 1-star reviews here on Amazon- I think Neato should focus more energy on actually bettering their sub-par customer service instead of perusing product reviews to leave syrupy comments simply referring disgruntled customers to their 1-800 number!

The robot itself performs well when functioning, but all the hassle that comes with it is worth neither your money or your time. I should have gotten a Roomba...

Input: After wearing out my third Hoover hard floor/carpet cleaner I was quite happy to try this one.  Unfortunately the squeegie (essential for hard floor cleaning) would not even attach.  A call to Hoover brought a quick response that they would send a new squeegie.  It arrived eight days later and did attach, but not with a "snap" as mentioned in the manual and the Hoover site video.  I began to clean the tile floor; after a few swipes the squeegie came off.  Tried several times with the same outcome.  I had a prolonged call with the Hoover support line; the agent kept indicating I hadn't put the squeegie on correctly.  She suggested that I should take the machine to the service center (70 miles away, I turned that idea down), and then said I could take it to a local appliance dealer to have them show me how to attach the squeegie.  After telling her I had read the manual twice and watched the Hoover how-to video, plus had my engineer husband read the manual and watch the video, and he had no better luck attaching the squeegie so that it would stay on.  She then told me she would transfer me to someone that would give me further assistance.  When the new person got online, she not only did not know anything about the situation but said she asked if I was a dealer because that was who she works with.  She transferred me back to customer assistance and another agent who offered to send a new squeegie.  I did not want to go past the 30 day return period, and did not have any hope that a third squeegie would solve the problem, so declined that offer.  I asked if they had any clips or other means of keeping the squeegie attached and got a negative reply.  I told her I would be giving up and returning the product.
Amazon made it very simple to return the product; they deserve a five star review for that process.
Addendum:  About 30 minutes after completing the customer support phone conversations, the first agent called to let me know Hoover would replace the appliance.  I did not take advantage of their offer, but instead gave up on a hard floor cleaner/carpet cleaner and purchased a different brand vacuum/steam mop....which does work.

Input: I wouldn't recommend ordering this if you're going to need it urgently within a week or two. Otherwise, it's definitely worth your money.

I was given this package as a gift, and began to assemble it the day before I planned to brew, only to find that it was missing most of the parts. I had the chiller with welded GHT fittings, one female GHT to 3/8" hose barb fitting, hose clamps, and a single hose (meaning I was missing everything on the left side of the main product image). It was unusable in this state, since the proper fittings are required for you to hook the hose to the chiller.

I let customer service know, and they were happy to ship me out the replacement parts. I was excited to receive the parts, but upon inspection, one of the replacement fittings had a 1/2" barb, meaning it was mismatched with the rest of the kit and wouldn't fit in the hose provided. I contacted them again and they got it right the 3rd time (and threw in some free crown caps at my request).

The product itself is great, especially if you get everything you need in one go. Not having the hoses clamped to the chiller makes it easier to move around, and less likely that you'll damage the hoses by having them dangle over the edge of the pot while you're putting it in for the last couple minutes of the boil. The faucet adapter was key for me as well, since I don't have access to a garden hose. And finally, having two 12' hoses ups your chances of being able to set the kettle where you need it while staying in range of the nearest faucet.

Input: So far, so good after 10 days and being used bunches of times.

I have severe arthritis and cannot use a traditional vacuum cleaner.  I have someone who comes in and cleans for me every other week, but needless, to say, the floors get quite dirty.  We have 2 cats, 1 dog and a large parrot in a house with mostly area rugs.

I had a roomba until it got to the end of its life about 6 months ago.  I chose the Neato over a new Roomba based upon the many reviews here on Amazon, and am pleased with my purchase so far.

1.  First of all, it cleans very well.  I believe the Roomba cleaned a little better in terms of getting every little crumb off of the floor, but the more powerful suction on the Neato means it grabs more deeply on carpets.

2.  Emptying the dustbin on the Neato is much easier, and it's a cinch to lift off of the top, which is easier on arthritic hands.  It just lifts right off of the top - you don't need to pull it off of the side like the Roomba (or at least the one that I had).

3.  This cleaner rocks on carpet.  Even with a bi-weekly Dyson vacuuming, there was still a lot of pet hair in our wall-to-wall bedroom carpet.  I ran the Neato about 4 times to get it all out, and voila, the carpet looks great.

4.  I believe the Neato is quite a bit louder than the Roomba, but this is a question of personal perception.

I am pleased with my Neato, and will wait to see if I run into battery or other issues that reviewers have commented about.  I gave it 4 stars because of its performance on floors.  If a few crumbs here or there don't bother you, than it would be a 5.

Input: So I rely a lot on reviews so I wanted to add input.  I really had a lot of hope for this machine.  A self-docking robot that vacuums and mops for around $200 is a crazy good price.  Here is what I discovered from my purchase...
The product did not work.  It kept saying, "check underneath sensor."  I followed the instructions in the manual multiple times and cleaned the sensors.  No luck.  After about 30 minutes, I finally got it to work.
I found the device cleans very well.  It's a bit louder than I expected, but not terrible.  It did a very good job cleaning my tile and laminate flooring for about 20 minutes.  The vacuum picked up a lot of material and the machine is heavy enough to scrub well with the pad.  The pad was filthy when I stopped it and the floor was surprisingly clean in that area.
The machine is very easy to maintain (unlike some comments I read on here.). The pad simply sticks underneath and the vacuum debris pops out quickly for easy disposal.
Once I stopped the machine, I could not get it working again.  The reviews are true that the company is out of business so if you get this device, you better spend the extra $20 for Amazon's service protection plan.
In sum, not a great experience but since I had it such a short time, Amazon is refunding my purchase, no problem.  I was impressed enough with the price and cleaning ability to try buying it again with my refunded money.  I'm hoping I just got a dud and my next experience will be better.  I'm not expecting much.  I figure if I can get this to run a year or two it will be well worth the money.  I just can't bring myself to spent $500-600 on one of these devices that only mops or only vacuums.

UPDATE:  so robot #2 arrived today.  This one seems to work.  It spent about 30 minutes on its initial charge moving about and cleaning the floor.  It cleans and scrubs well and left the floors looking great.  At times it seems confused and moves slow, but you just have to let it do its thing.  One problem is when it finished and tried to find its dock, it couldn't seem to figure it out.  It headed right for the area which was promising, and even ran into the dock, but just kept spinning and moving around the area.  After 10 minutes I couldn't take it anymore and just put it on the charger myself.  I had read that it couldn't seem to self charge in another review and am sad to confirm that...at least so far.

So, if you are looking for a nice little robot that cleans tile, hardwood, etc. well at a very cheap price, this is for you.  If you are looking for a $800 dollar, self docking system that you hardly have to touch, this isn't it.  Just make sure you buy the warranty.

Input: The item description claims that it can handle up to a 25V power supply. I tried running this board with a 24V power supply and one of the bypass capacitors blew up spectacularly. Turns out that although the driver chips can handle the voltage (I think they're rated up to 36V), this board uses bypass capacitors with a 16V maximum working voltage. To be on the safe side you wouldn't want to run right up to the max rating, but you should be fine with a 12V supply or possibly even a 14.8V LiPo battery pack.

If you're feeling adventurous you could desolder the two caps in question (C7 and C8 on the board) and replace them with higher voltage rated caps with the same footprint to beef up the max voltage.

Other than the blowing up issue, the board works fine.

Maybe someone from Glide Gear would be kind to comment if I pushed the rig too hard with 15lbs of counterweight?

Input: I haven't been able to confirm the longevity of the light as yet (I've had one other that failed after a few months of regular use), but it does appear to work initially, once connected to a 120V plug.  There is about a 1 or 2 second delay from when the power is turned on and when  the light reaches full intensity (BRIGHT).  On the one I received, the AC wire colors were blue and red, which translated to white / black  (neutral / hot) in the U.S..  In the plug, I connected the blue wire to the silver color screw (neutral wire), and the red wire to the brass color screw (hot wire) in the plug.  The ground terminal of the plug was connected to the green / yellow wire.

As reported by others, thought there is a ground wire (green / yellow) on the short (6 inch) pigtail, it isn't connected to the metal housing in the one I received. This wire was too short (inside the housing) to ground directly. It was necessary to  connect it to the base of the rear housing (by removing one of screws), connecting a wire under it and connecting a longer wire to reach the ground wire on the pigtail going into the voltage converter.  I have a soldering iron, solder and used it to insure a good joint to ground (between the longer ground wire and the terminal at the end of the green / yellow wire).  Particularly when you have a metal housing, grounding is necessary for safety. The lights don't appear to be listed (e.g. UL), which isn't surprising when the housing isn't grounded.

As was recommended in other reviews, I removed the glass cover and inner reflector and inspected the mounting of the LED element.  Though there were 4 screws and there was thermal compound on the rear of the LED element, the screws were not down tight. The screws are flat head M3 x 0.5 pitch x 4 mm.  The inner reflector only used 2 screws (same size screw as on the LED element) and got a couple more at the local hardware store.  I made sure the screws were tightened down on the LED, and made sure I had a good (though thin) later of thermal compound.  If you have a LED element that fails and you have a soldering iron, you can replace the LED with one from Amazon or Ebay [currently $9 to $8 for 50W element].  I'm using mine as a plant light operated with a timer, but have also used them for outside illumination.

Input: I had super high hopes for this vacuum. This is my first roomba. I thought it would have a methodical way of cleaning, but there are several reasons why this vacuum doesn't work like I had expected. Here's the short: the question is vacuum yourself in just minutes or endure loud vacuum background noise all day long by a vacuum that gets confused and dies before going home to recharge itself. I thought this would be something that would simplify my life, but it's more like having a third child...it's noisy and one more thing to watch over.

Cons:
This robot supposedly goes home to recharge before it dies. The very first time I used it, it died and I had to carry it back to home base. Because it died midway through the job, it forgot what it had already done and restarted everything from the beginning when it restarted. After redoing what it had already done, it started to die again and tried to go home  but couldn't attach to home base, making confused circles right in front of it. Again, I had to carry it and manually attach it to home base. So the first 4 hours of cleaning, it only cleaned my dining room. In 4 hours of my own time, I could have hand scrubbed each and every tile and cleaned every inch of grout in the dining room along with polished all the furniture to a high shine.

This thing is loud. Shame on me for thinking it would be something that could run seamlessly in the background. Not so...really loud like a full size dyson and needs to be something that I can run when I'm not home (although I am rarely gone the whole day and it needs the WHOLE day to finish. More on this below).

Short battery life. The roomba starts with a full bettery and runs longest on the full battery. When it dies, it recharges and starts again on it's own, but runs for about 45 minutes before needing to go home to recharge again for another 90 minutes. NINETY MINUTES. Then it restarts the job. This goes on all day long.

Takes the entire day to get the job done. I have about 1000 square feet on the first floor where roomba was working. After EIGHT hours of working and recharging, it was still not done with the job. Finally at 10:30pm and bedtime, I had to simply cancel the job because it's too loud to run in the night (well it can't see well in the night anyways). 8 hours is a long time to endure loud persistent vacuum noise on the main level on and off all day. I'm curious to know how long it would have taken to get the actual job completely "done" had I let it keep going. 12 hours? 15 hours? 1000 sq ft takes me all of 10 minutes to vacuum on my own. The question is truly do it yourself in 5 minutes or endure loud vacuuming noise all day long. Maybe if you leave all day for work this may be the thing for you. If you work from home like I do... maybe not the best choice.

Input: This  made in China metal platform truck is sold under various manufacturer names on Amazon.com.  I doubt if the truck is heavy duty, in that it could stand up to punishment, but it is definitely heavy, weighing about 40 pounds. The only way to get the truck out of the crushed box was to cut away all sides and just pulling it out. You have to attach the four wheels yourself.  This involves pulling out four bolts attached to the bottom of the truck for each wheel, along with their flimsy locking washers. You then have  to attach each 5" wheel to the platform using the bolts and washers. The threaded part of the bolt is only about 3/4" with a hex head, perhaps too short. A socket wrench should do the job, but getting the bolts back into platform both tight and straight is no easy matter. The wheels do not allow for much headroom, so getting the socket to work properly becomes quite a chore. I had to resort to a set of pliers to complete the  tightening, which wasn't always as tight or straight as I would like. With the short bolts there is also a strong possibility the wheels could become loose or fall off after several uses.

Given the weight of this truck, a good deal of the Amazon cost is for additional shipping charges. If you could pick it up at a local store it would cost about $40-$50 plus the sales tax. Also returning this monster to Amazon would be quite a chore. (But I am contemplating  doing it anyway.) Buying  a platform truck at your local home improvement store  may be a more rational choice. Look for a Rubbermaid  brand truck. Their wheels just pop in and lock in place. No bolts necessary; and they weigh far less than this one.

Input: I was excited to get this mug for such a great price, but when I finally received it I was extremely disappointed. As the old adage goes...you get what you pay for. When a price seems too good to be true, it usually is. This mug is far to heavy for me to hold and even manage to drink from.  Now, I recently had a complete right shoulder repair where I nearly severed my entire right shoulder in a competitive snowboarding accident.  However this should not affect me drinking from the mug as I go through my therapy program. The mug seems unbalanced at the top which I believe aids in making it heavier.  When the handle is attached, it adds a significant amount of heft to the mug making it more difficult to lift. I did not receive the stainless steel straw I was supposed to, so when I lift this mug to drink from it it feels like it is smacking me in the face make it extremely difficult and unpleasant.

I did receive the straw brush but the bristles are missing from the end of the brush by .33 inch from the tip of the brush. When I attempted to use this brush to clean one of my smaller stainless steel straws, the brush had difficulty fitting into the straw probably because of the missing bristles. The straw would not bend at all around the bend of the straw and I was extremely disappointed that I felt that I had to try and force the brush into the straw which was a struggle for me.

When I have tried to place this in my cup holder it does not fit well and the handle hangs over into the second cup holder.  I drive a nice upgraded SUV and this should be the least of my issues.

I previously owned the 30 oz. Yeti Rambler and used it with zero difficulties. Unfortunately, the mug was confiscated during my last move by a family member.  I was trying to avoid buying another Yeti, but I may have to eventually give in and do so.

I gave this review two stars only because I received a great price on the product. Other than the price, there is not one positive thing that I can say about this mug. It's definitely too bulky for my female hands and far too heavy and unbalanced for me to use. A straw would have helped, but since I didn't receive one, I can only review based on the way the product was received.  I will give this to my dad since he will have more use for it rather than returning it, since it's not worth the hassle.

Input: Since I spend a great deal of time flying for work, I decided it was time to upgrade my cheap headphones for a better quality set instead of the cheap pair I usually have or the ones provided by airlines (can never tell if they actually sanitize them).

After a great deal of research reading reviews by audiophiles, I decided to try the MH40's out along with the Beoplay H6, Beoplay H8, MH30. numerous Beats models and what ever model Bose what available at the local Apple Store.

I made sure to listen to the same songs on each pair to determine the sound quality that I liked as well as which offered the best comfort (I wear glasses) and muffled out background sounds. Luckily it was a busy day at the Apple Store so there was a very good amount of background noise created by all the other shoppers.

Out of all of the pairs I tried, I loved the MH40's the best with the H6's a close second. The Bose much like other users have noted had a very bland or muted sound quality no doubt due to the noise cancelling feature. Everything else I tried was too bass heavy which I do not like. The H8's actually produced a certain low frequency that almost immediately cased discomfort in my ears and a headache.

Pro's that made me decide on the MH40's:

* Extremely light, comfortable and does not disturb or effect my glasses
* I love the sound quality, works great with everything I listen to (Classical, Blues, Rock, R&B (non-Hip Hop), and the variety of Electronic music)
* Sounds great with movies as well
* Comes with 2 cables that can be removed in case they are damaged
* Well made with great materials (still have to see how they hold up long term)
* Breath well, no sweating around my ears even after wearing them for an extended period in a warm store
* Has an easy to reach mute button on the right side
* Love the retro look

Con's or things I did not like:

* $399 price (but I prefer quality so expect to pay more)
* Lacks a hard case, only a cloth bag (especially for this price point, a $20 hard case like the Geekria could have been included)

Over all I look forward to enjoying the MH40's on my upcoming flights this year.

One quick note, if you are like me and tend not to read instructions before using devices, make sure to plug the cord into the left side and not the right side otherwise you will notice issues with the sound quality since the right side is meant as an output only connection.

For Mac users, I tested the MH40's on my iMac, 17" Mac Book Pro and 11" Mac Book Air as well as both of my iPhones (6 & 6+) and found that they work great with all of them (including the inline volume controls).

If you are thinking of purchasing a pair of MH40's but also want a hard case to protect them, check out the Greekria case I purchased and wrote a review on as well.

Input: I am one of the people who was late onto the iPhone scene, but before I finally got mine I did some extensive research on accessories. Having heard about the short battery life, mostly due to the phone's capabilities, I decided a backup battery/charger was a must. I researched a number of batteries/chargers and finally decided I liked the Kensington Battery Pack and Charger.

I have not been disappointed. Here are the things I have liked about this battery pack and charger:

1. You can charge the iPhone and battery pack at the same time, which is nice if you use the battery pack on a daily basis.
2. You get an extra iPhone data cable (iPhone/iPod hookup on one end and a USB plug on the other). When I'm at work I just use this cable to charge my iPhone from my laptop's USB.
3. Using the supplied accessories you can charge just the iPhone or just the battery. Basically, you are getting another iPhone DC Adapter.
4. The battery charges the phone almost completely while still on. I have had a number of instances where my battery was at 10%-20%. I plugged in the battery pack, while leaving the phone on and I was able to get my charge up to about 90% in about 2-3 hours. If I turned off the phone, I'm sure I would have gotten the full charge, but 90% while still being able to use the phone is great.

I have very few complaints about the battery pack, other than it would be nice if it were smaller. Even so, the battery pack is smaller than the iPhone and a little bit thinner. So, in the grand scheme of things there could be much bigger draw backs.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with the purchase. For the money, you can't go wrong considering all the extras you get for the price. I've seen a lot of other chargers go for more, which didn't even come close to features and accessories.

Here are some tips to help you when your iPhone is low on battery until you get your Kensington Battery Pack and Charger:

- Decrease the brightness of the screen
- Not using Wifi, turn it off under settings
- Not using Bluetooth, turn it off under settings
- Not using GPS (localization services), turn it offer under settings
- Set Fetch New Data option to Manually

Input: About me:

I'm a Computer Programmer/Photographer who uses a Laptop for coding, DSLR to take pictures and Good music player to listen to music. Simply put, I use a equipment for what it's meant for (and the manufacturer is good at making it).  I'm not a musician but still have a deep love for any music.

For people who aren't anywhere close to getting a Bose:

So if you're the kind to use a cellphone to take "awesome" pictures, DSLR to take videos and Dock Station to have Alarm and Radio, you rather go for one of those Dock Stations which has the fancy LED Display, Radio and Alarm clocks but sounds distorted when you try bumping it up beyond 60% Volume (basically Jack of All trades, master of none). They're still worth every penny if you need a Multi-purpose gadget. No complaints there. You can stop reading now.

Those who are seriously considering a Bose Sounddock:

Just remember, with Great Quality comes Great Price. :( If your love for music is greater than your desire to save a couple of hundred dollars of hard earned money, then this is my 2 cent. "Buy it, blindly" (else) "Go to a store nearby and compare the quality of every Dock ever manufactured. 2 hours later, you'd still buy this one" Why? Pure "Music Magic". The SDP blew away every Dock on the shelf (of similar portable size).

Sounddock Portable (or) Soundlink???

Bluetooth is certainly a nice thing to have in a Dock Station, but Unfortunately SDP doesn't. But that isn't a deal-breaker and definitely not a reason you need to go for a Soundlink blindly. Soundlink sure is more portable (weight/dimension wise), but definitely slightly less on the volume front. And both Sounddock ($100 off) and Soundlink are same in price now ($299). I choose volume over portability and to fix the lack of Bluetooth, all I did was get a Sounddock Bluetooth Adapter for $15 off Amazon. So now, I have a truly portable SDP which can play music from almost anything using Bluetooth/IphoneDock/3.5mm AUX.
I already have the Bose MIE2i mobile headset so I really wasn't surprised over the clarity of the SDP or the Ergonomics of Bose products. What really surprised me is the difference the Waveguide speaker technology has over other Docks. No matter which end of the room you are sitting in, it almost feels like sitting in the best seat of a Music concert... Pleasing to the ears. I still haven't jacked it up to max volume cos it's so loud, I don't want the apartment neighbors to complain. Ideal portable player for outdoor camping, BBQ, indoor parties/workout etc. It just doesn't play music... it gets you into the feel of it too.  Bose has also paid attention to small practical problems of a Remote Control and frequently tangled up wires. You'll understand what I mean when you buy one.

Only possible Design Flaw I noticed till now:

I was a bit shocked at first, when I realized I had to keep adjusting the Iphone on the Dock for loose connection. Then I realized I hadn't docked in the iphone properly and fixed it again properly (need to apply more pressure than you would want to, on a $400 system). The Dock station pin looks a bit flimsy and MIGHT wear out eventually with heavy usage. But doesn't matter to me cos I'm only planning to use it with Bluetooth mostly.

My only reason for concern before buying is that, Amazon shows this product was launched in April 18, 2005 (atleast the earliest version of it). But after a lot of research I realized that this product (new version) is just 10 years ahead of the competition and the rest are still catching up. $100 off on a Bose might mean the next version is coming soon but who cares... I ain't no professional musician and I don't think my ears can differentiate anything that sounds better/crisper/nicer than this one. 5 stars!

Input: This is an incredibly cheap tablet, which I feared would not work well but so far it done everything I expected a tablet to do. It came already 80% charged, and though the instructions say that you need to charge it for 10 hours before first using it, I used it after five or so hours when the battery showed 100% ready. It comes with a white USB cord and I charged this quickly and easily using my USB wall charger.

The tablet is smaller than others I've seen, about the size of a paperback book and very thin. This makes it great for toting in a backpack or handbag. Needless to say it's great for reading eBooks and watching videos. It takes up little room and is perfect for travel. The blue plastic casing feels a little cheap, however, so I'd be careful with it (this is the only sign, for me, that it's a less expensive tablet).

The touchscreen is predictably sensitive and I had no problems searching the Web and changing the wallpaper (it now boasts a photo of my current cat, Maggie). A few times I had to tap it a little harder, but nothing unusual about that - a lot of tablets have funky moments.

On a single charge, it worked well for three days, though I didn't use it for more than an hour at a time. By the third day, the battery power was down to 34%, but I think that's pretty good, especially if you're using it to supplement a smartphone while you are out and about.

Another thing that's cool - this iRULU is fully up to date and will let you download the latest apps out there. My smartphone has an outdated browser, which makes downloading new apps a headache unless I upgrade. With iRULU I was able to download the newest stuff, including that maddeningly addictive cat collector game, Neko Atsume.

Note: the user should be aware that this tablet is very Google-friendly, and in order to use some of the functions I had to give Google permission to sync the tablet with my Gmail and provide Google with all that personal information that it so greedily collects. Once you do this, it's a breeze to use, including the speak-only Google Now app, which allows you to search the web by voice alone.

In short, all the functions worked smoothly. The only area where I was disappointed was the "Camera" function. I tried to take photos of my cat, but they all looked blurry and not very sharp. I tried again and the same result. So, not impressed with this part of it.

Otherwise this tablet offers a lot of great features for very little money. Only time will tell if it is durable as well.

I received this in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

I recommend this product.

Input: I'd done the research, checked the benchmarks, and read many a technical review before finally deciding on this card. I've had great experiences with ASUS in general, and their 680s have been getting good reviews. I have a really good gaming desktop, but it's 3 years old, and while I really enjoy my 480GTXes, the 680 has been a dramatic improvement.

FITTING IN
If you're looking to drop one or more of these in your computer case, you definitely want to check the measurements, as this card is LONG. It is just a tiny bit longer than my 480GTXes, but inside a case that may make all the difference, so check the dimensions before buying. I've also noticed that the heat-pipes stand just a tiny bit taller than the 480GTX, so if it's already close quarters between your side panel and your current card, check measurements. The card has two 6-pin power plugs. If you have 8-pin plugs, most allow you to separate the last two pins for just this purpose, but if for some reason you don't, then ASUS provides you with a power 'Y' cable that will convert two Molex (4-pin) plugs into one 6-pin video plug.

FIRING UP
The ASUS 680 GTX is all about small improvements leading to big gains: the two fans atop the heatsink are large, but the fan motors have noise dampening built into them. There were issues with the 480s getting heat trapped between the end of the card and the back of the case, so slight changes to the shape of the vents have fixed this problem. Because there is a monstrous amount of metal hanging upside down off the card for heat blocks, fans, and pipes, the backplate is the size of the card and the countersunk screws tightly hold everything in place. NVidia have introduced a technology called GPU Boost that raises and lowers performance on demand and will eagerly push the clock speed and voltage envelopes while keeping an eye on temperatures. ASUS also adds a software utility that makes it very easy for you to raise the bar yourself: you can set voltages, clock speeds, fan sensitivity and speeds, to all have a higher floor. Unfortunately, you cannot disable or control NVidia's GPU Boost at this time--Tom's Hardware groused that this made managing their benchmarking sessions fairly difficult--but if you use the ASUS software to adjust settings you may find you have some control over how low the usage goes.

FLYING HIGH
Installation was as cut and dried as it should be: uninstall all NVidia software, shut down, swap old cards for new, check connections, power up and install the new drivers. One reboot later and I was ready to rock. After popping into Skyrim and trying 2D and 3DVision, I was amazed at how much 'sharper' everything appeared to be: not just a framerate improvement, but a kind of clarity that reminds me of an eye doctor's office: "Better or worse?" "Oh, man...definitely BETTER." Skyrim, Bioshock Infinite, and Planetside 2 all ran smooth as silk at 1920 x 1080 and of course there was not a hiccup when dropping down to 1280x720 for some 3D gaming.*

I haven't run every performance benchmark I can think of yet, but I did run Futuremark's latest "Extreme" benchmarking test for games. With the 480s, I was above-average, but not Superman. With the 680s, I instantly hit the top score and was 1,000 marks above my nearest competitor. The fact that I can run anything at the highest possible settings is overkill, and I think based on benchmarks I've read that the fact that this is a 4GB card makes a substantial difference: the 2GB is quite an excellent card, this one just gives the GPU so much more room to play.

If you have the money, and like me you were watching for the 700 series to put some downward price pressure on the 680s, the ASUS 4GB GTX680-DC2-4GD5 is definitely a huge bang...it's just still a somewhat sizeable amount of bucks.

Tech Specs:
Intel Core i7 Xtreme 980X Processor (six cores), overclocked to 4.2GHz using Intel Performance Tuning
3 x 4GB DDR3 gaming RAM, overclocked using Intel XMP
Samsung 830 Series SSD with Windows 8 Professional 64-bit installed
4 x 1TB WD Caviar Black (RAID 5) for programs
2 x ASUS 4GB GTX680-DC2-4GD5 graphics cards (SLI enabled) rendering to a Vizio 46" 3D HDTV

*a word about online games like Planetside 2: no matter what machine or how fast a connection, if you are in a world with a lot of people and a lot of combat, you may see slowdowns that have nothing to do with your hardware and everything to do with the game servers trying to manage all that traffic. When Sony sold 'fireworks' guns on the 4th of July weekend, my Planetside 2 sessions became a mess of massive battles combined with groups of people standing around shooting off fireworks all over the place...everyone's performance dropped.

Input: Well, just under three months of using the nuvi 265WT, and I returned it to Costco. For the first time Garmin has let me down. I am truly disappointed - the first out of 6 Garmins I have owned (fitness watches 301, and now 305; Street Pilot 330; Nuvi 350; eTrex Vista, and this 265WT). I gave it every opportunity to come through, to deliver on the promise of an improved nuvi, but nearly every aspect of this unit is a step behind my dear, departed (gave it away!) nuvi 350:

1. Confounding  Interface - As an example, they moved the custom POI from the Favorites, down another level to EXTRAS. Why? In the 350, selecting Favorites gave a list of Recently Selected, Saved Favorites, and Custom POIs, if there were any installed. You now have to go to another level, on the second screen (page down) for EXTRAS, and the only extra is Custom POIs. Why?

2. Exasperating Interface - It always annoyed me (even on my 350) that there was no quick way to get back to the main menu, or the map, after having to do a menu dive for POIs or, even worse, entering an address. "BACK, BACK, BACK, BACK." Until you hit the main menu and are able to select "Display Map." Now, if you are programming a multiple stop trip, you have to enter the first destination, wait for the trip to calculate, and then begin to go back through the menus to add the next destination. Once again, "BACK, BACK, BACK, BACK" through the menus. But now, there is a trip in progress, and down in the lower left corner of the main menu screen, the same place that the BACK button was, is the STOP button. Hit that corner one too many times, and your trip is cancelled - start again. Exasperating.

3.  Traffic - this was THE primary reason for me to upgrade. The free traffic reports directly to your GPS. I travel 90 minutes one way on my commute. A lot of roads and good traffic reports are my best friend. And reports on radio are not good - you have to wait 10-15 minutes for them to come up, and then they are 20-30 minutes behind. I was hoping the real time updates to my GPS would be the ticket. And they would be IF THEY WERE EVER RIGHT. I know many people out here have said they are great. My trip entails the Garden State Parkway, and sometimes the New Jersey Turnpike. Two major roads in a major metropolitan area. The traffic reports are so bad, I simply ignore them. I stopped getting mad because the reports were wrong; I now get mad when they are right. Which is RARE. To those readers living in NJ, try the NJ 511 service. 511 from your cell phone, and you get the most current traffic reports. Fantastic; it has taken the place of radio and the nuvi.

4. Sudden Muting - I turn on the GPS, and no sound. I have to go to volume, adjust the volume (up or down, it doesn't matter) and then the muting ends. This happens regularly. Others have reported the same problem.

5. Helium Voice - Every once and awhile, the GPS stop responding.  Touch the screen and it slowly comes out of a "slumber" - only to awaken with lungs full of helium. They voice has turned high-pitched. Only a hard reset will fix it.

6. Bluetooth problems - if you setup a connection to your Bluetooth cell phone, but the phone is not in range when you turn on the GPS, you get a connection failure message (for example, I get in the car, start up the GPS, go back into the house to get something and come back out after the GPS has started). No problem. Menu dive DEEP into system settings to set up the connection. The GPS will lock up EVERYTIME. I have learned that I just do not turn on the GPS until I know my phone will stay in range.

7. Strange Direction Changes - I go home the same way everyday, along the GSP. The only way is by NJ 208. Typically, the 265WT will correctly send me down 208 to NJ 4 and then the GSP. But strangely, every once and awhile, it will send me down back roads, through Patterson NJ. Or at least try to. I know enough now to simply pass that instructed turn off and it will re-calculate. Originally I thought it was because Navigation setting had "Avoid Traffic" as the default. (Which in and of itself is a problem - why would that be the default, especially when "Avoid Traffic" is an option when reviewing traffic reports). But it is not the problem - I long ago set that option off. That route, even on the best of days, is at least 10 minutes longer, although a few miles shorter (and no, I do not have the GPS set to SHORTEST ROUTE).

8. Advertisements - I do not mind the ads, and I understand they pay for the "free" traffic reports. But I have, over the 3 months I owned the 265WT, seen the same ad - Best Western! That's it! 3 hours a day, 5 days a week, and the same lousy ad over and over. And it pops up all over the place, not just when you are on the map looking at the directions. Do a search - there's an ad; select a POI - there's an ad; check the settings - there's an ad. The ONLY ad. Best Western. And, to my mind, selecting the ad should make it disappear. I saw the ad, selected it, read it, now GO AWAY. Nope - keeps popping up. Over and over and over again.

What can I say, up to this unit, I loved my Garmins. Before I sprung for this GPS, I considered just keeping my trusty 350 and updating the maps. But the lure of wide screens, bluetooth and traffic reports vs. spending $60 for a map upgrade, well, I sprung for the new. And gave away my 350. And regret that decision.

Hey, there area lot of 4-5 star reviews for this GPS, some by first time Garmin or GPS owners, some by long timers. Maybe there was a problem with mine unit, but based upon the feedback read here about similar problems, I think not.

Some might say, why not contact Garmin support? Well, the reason is, if there was a problem, they would want the unit for repair/replace. The problems:

1. I pay for shipping
2. I am out a GPS until they repair or replace
3. The replacement is almost ALWAYS a refurb - trade my brand new unit for a repaired? I don't think so
4. Costco has a great return policy - no questions, 90 days. If I exchange it, I get a new unit, or I can return it for a full refund. Which is what I did - get a refund.

I have my money back, no nuvi 350, and I am searching again for a new GPS. The 755 looks tempting, but I see similar problems with THAT unit too! I may have to go to the dark side - and consider TomTom or Magellan. I hope there is a Garmin out there that fits the bill.

Input: I have purchased Poetic cases for everybody in my family over the past few years. They used to be fantastic, and are still holding up for everyone. Everyone, except me.

I have been so annoyed by this case I needed to post a review. The first one I received had gouges out of the cover, horrible condition. Sent it back.

On the second one, I use my iPad about 15 times a week, never in portrait mode, and I never drop my gadgets.

The first crack started about two weeks after purchase, but it was small so I didn't care, it was more, "Wow the reviewers on Amazon were right, this has weak plastic". Then, two nights ago, I'm holding it in portrait mode reading news, and plastic pieces start falling off the corners under my hands. Absolutely unacceptable. Now, whenever I hold my iPad, I'm holding sharp edges of plastic. Beware of the weak plastics Poetic used in this model of case.

Two stars because the product itself is great, but they really tried to skimp on the plastic in this model compared to other models. Charge me more money for a more robust plastic- I love your product- but don't give me some flimsy thing that degrades your brand because it can't be used for more than a few months.

Unfortunately, I'm probably going to buy another one because they're so slim and the cheapest, relatively high quality case I have seen.

I do like the design, so it allowed me to put so much into it, but the stitching did hold up. This bag needs a mechanical fastener, like heavy duty snaps, instead of the magnetic posts. The layout is great. It has all the right pouches and compartments in all the right places, yet, the assembled product needs heavier duty thread, fasteners, and zippers. Makes me want to make my own bag. Needs memory foam too. It is comfortable as it stands. If you do not plan on putting more than 3-4lbs in this, you should get a couple of years out of it. In sum, great design, poor craftsmanship.

Input: I've had mine since September and took it along on a short vacation to Michigan and Florida.  I came home with maybe 150 images set mostly on Aperture priority for the trip.  Thinking the f8 setting may help the sharpness I can't say it helped at all.  Possibly the dof changed but I'll have to push it a little harder with some more challenging dof requirements.  As others have mentioned the GPS does draw down the battery quite fast especially in log mode in a couple of short days for me. I did drop the camera once onto concrete from 2 ft or so.  It damaged the metal band near the flash but otherwise all works well.

Pros:  Lightning fast start-up and shutter response.
The GPS is handy.
Very good low light performance.
 Not a bad price point.

Cons: The GPS is handy but slow to acquire a location (  100ft) and draws down the battery fast.
Weak flash.
Colors get muddy in the fine details, yellows and green especially.  I find this true in my other Canon Power shot A710-IS as well and the fall colors in Michigan especially took a hit.
Edit:  October 2013.  I've started getting lens errors occasionally and have to power off the camera to "fix" it.

Edit:  March 2014.  Getting "lens errors" continuously now and the camera shuts off.  So I guess it's all over for this one. 2 1/2 years was it's life span.
  I've down graded the rating to two stars.

Input: I got this because I needed a basic router that could handle multiple connections and not break under the strain.  I needed all 4 ports for a desktop (gigabit Ethernet destroys wireless for ping on multiplayer games!), PS3 (same reason), and two networked printers.  I also have three or four devices that connect wirelessly.  This router was easy to set up, had good security options and seemed to work fine for a couple of months.  But I found that YouTube on the wireless connection with a Windows Update running means that my Android smartphone net speed slows to a crawl.  I pay for a 20mbps connection and Speedtest shows that this isn't giving it to me.

This router cannot handle multiple connections very well.  Downloading large open-source code packages via P2P networks chokes the pipe to a crawl OR kills it altogether until an unplug and restart.  I have a 1000 square foot apartment with this in one bedroom and when I'm on the other side of the apartment, I don't get full signal.

This is a good basic router for a single user who primarily streams YouTube or Netflix to one laptop at a time.  If you are a power user or really need good range, then you need to spend more money on a N600 or N900-level router.  Additionally, since this router does not specify compatibility with IPv6, a more expensive router might be more future proof.

I never used the USB port so I can't comment on it.  I never flashed Tomato to it, so I am not sure if that it a good thing or not.  I just know that this router is not really optimized to take advantage of superfast modem speeds.

Input: This is my first ipod. All over, it is a well done product. A lot of cool apps to keep you from boredom. But this ipod as a media player...it's just average or even below average in some cases.

My other MP3 player are the Sony Ericsson i750 & Sonly Clie TJ37, they blow this ipod away when it comes to the sound quality. It's hard to believe there's no EQ for ipod Touch, sound quality is flat as the result of all genres play on one flat EQ setting. iTunes 8 is extremely slow on Windows XP doesn't help much neither.

Video is cool, instant access to youtube. Once again, lack of video controls. It only has brightness control, no contrast (I might be wrong on this)

Pro:
- Near perfection integration between iPod & iTune, very easy to use
- Display lyrics on screen (if lyric is loaded on iTune)
- Superb user interface
- Accelerometer really brings fun out of the games, kinda like Wii.
- Supports microphone, which enables to use VOIP such as Skype over wifi
- A tone of cool apps and a tone of junk apps

Cons:
- Too large and fragile to be an everyday portable MP3 player, unless you have a man bag. lol.  One drop, it is gone. I've dropped my i750 many times and it still rocks.
- Average sound quality with no EQ support. What is Apple thinking?
- Turtle speed with iTune 8 on Windows XP
- Average earphone
- expensive accessory. $15.00-30.00 for a piece of thin silicon skin that is made in China?

If you want a solid and durable MP3 player, this is not the one for you. But if you want an average MP3 player with lots apps to keep you entertained, then this is a great gadget for you!

Update 3/08:
Good news, it does have an EQ. Bad news, it is buried in the Setting->Music->EQ.The difference between the EQ settings is barely noticeable, it's better than none.

It also a bug, its clock will go crazy when it connects with the PC where iTunes 8 is already running. You have to make sure iTunes 8 is not running on the PC before plug in the USB, otherwise you have to set the clock each time.

Apple, iTunes movie rental is a great idea. But $3.99 for 24 hours on a tiny screen? Hmmm...you should have a 0.99 rental for iphone/ipod touch category.

Input: I have a thing for sleep keyboards. This one was a decent price and had decent reviews, so I thought I'd give it a shot.

Everything seemed well at first. I purchased it for my office, so I threw the box away after I thought I was satisfied with it, so it wasn't cluttering up my office (first mistake).

I instantly noticed that the keys seemed a bit hard to depress. This isn't a defect, but I think they require too much pressure than they should, and I feel it slightly decreases my typing speed.

Now, the problems. I've only had it for about a week, and multiple keys have started to squeek when I press them, especially the spacebar. It's not a problem, but it's an annoyance. I like a quiet keyboard, and squeeky keys don't accomplish that. Second, the "-" key is broken already. I first noticed it whenever I would type a "-" and it would come up with doubles. I didn't pay much attention to it at first, but after I investigated, it turns out the key is just broken. The slightest touch on the key without depressing it causes it to register, which typically results in doubles whenever I press it.

Overall it's a decent keyboard for the price though. However, if I still had the box, I would definitely return it, as it isn't very high quality. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. If you like a slim keyboard, I would spend the extra $20 or so and get a Logitech Illuminated Keyboard. I have that at home, and am very satisfied with it.

Input: CAD ZOE review

There are a tremendous number of USB recording microphones on the market now, ranging from cheap units designed for communications or gaming use, up to $600 (the MXL USB.009), and there may well be even more expensive USB microphones I'm not aware of. Most designed for home recording are in the $50-150 range, which is right where this unit falls.

The Yeti is small, kind of cute really. Its mostly plastic, with a few bit of metal where needed, like the threaded microphone stand insert in the base Most users, I suspect, will use the included tripod stand, which turns the ZOE into tabletop microphone.

I've had several USB microphones, but for the past few years I've been using the Blue Microphones Yeti for my home recording. To my ears, it sounds pretty good, and it tends to come in at or near the top in most comparison articles I've read. This new microphone from CAD is in the same approximate price range, so I thought comparing the two side by side would be useful.

Looking at the specs, the Yeti seems to have almost all the advantages. It has a wider frequency range (20Hz-20KHz, versus 50Hz-16KHz), along with the same resolution (16 bit) and the same sampling rate (48KHz). The CAD does boast a more powerful headphone amplifier (300mw vs 130mw) plus a processing chip that is said to improve the monitoring, but this doesn't affect recorded quality.

On the other hand, that extra 4KHz of audio range doesn't necessarily contribute much to recordings of voices, acoustic guitars, and a lot of other instruments. Some of the really legendary recording microphones, like the Neumann U-47, had a significant falloff above 15KHz.

One clear advantage of the Yeti is its switchable recording pattern- you can choose omnidirectional, unidirectional, or figure-8, which pretty much covers any recording application you can come up with. The CAD is limited to an omni pattern, which is great for most music recording, but might be limiting for other applications, like recording voices in a noisy environment.

What it really comes down to is the sound quality. How does the ZOE sound, compared to the more expensive Yeti? I set them up side-by-side and recorded a few different acoustic guitars, mandolin, and upright bass, using Garage Band on my MacBook Air.

Recording, what struck me was that the CAD ZOE has significant latency compared to the Yeti. Its not a lot, but its enough that you have to anticipate where the beat is when you're adding additional tracks or playing along to a drum beat. It shouldnt be a problem in non-music applications, though. ON playback, the ZOE sounded good, almost the same as the Yeti, really, through the old Sony headphones I was using. On double bass, the Yeti had better response on those low notes on the E string.

In summary, Id say the ZOE sounds pretty good, has a good headphone monitor amp built in, and for Skyping or similar uses it is not a bad choice. But Id have to say that for multitrack recording, podcasting, voiceover narration and similar uses the Yeti is a lot more microphone for not that much more. With heavier duty construction, multiple patterns, better low end response and the option of single-point stereo recording, the Yeti makes the CAD ZOE look like only a fair value in comparison.

Input: I bought this system mainly because of its price and the decent reviews across the web of the company. It is not a high end system but it will do for regular home surveillance.  I tested the product out of the box and everything I tested worked fine.  The cameras came on and the DVR was functional.  (did not test the system over the internet)  The IR is not the best outdoors but you get better IR inside the home due to the reflection of the IR light off the surfaces in the home.  The Cameras will do well for facial recognition within 10-20 feet this would be the typical range in which you'd expect to find that in this price range.

I gave this system 3 stars due to its ability to be tampered with and the fact the images of the cameras lead you astray.  I live in a ranch style home meaning I'm in a single story and I cannot place my cameras up high enough that they could not be tampered with easily.  The wires attached to the Camera for both power and video feed are exposed to the elements which leaves them highly susceptible to vandalism.  Other systems have a "vandal-proof"  design where it goes through the post and is covered.

The camera system should be enough of a deterrent but some criminals consider it a challenge and will look for blind spots or vulnerabilities.  I'd rather not welcome the challenge and make it easy.

Other than the mentioned security risk this system is a sound investment especially for internal building surveillance as well higher than one story mounting outdoors.  I'd recommend this purchase for people in those two situations that are looking for a cheap system for security surveillance.

Input: I got these Bluetooth over the ear headphones mostly for my husband, but I have used them a few times too. We have different sets we use for running and working out, and while I like those for that purpose, I wanted a pair that was a little more comfortable. I just don't like the earbud kind as much so these really appealed to me. We've had them about a week and a half now and I've been able to use them a handful of times.

I love the size and weight. They're not so light that they feel cheap and flimsy, but not so heavy that they're cumbersome. The band is adjustable to fit many head sizes and the actual headphone portion is an average size. There's a light to easily indicate when the unit is on, which is helpful. The included directions were more than sufficient and getting the headphones paired with our phones was fast and easy. I haven't used them during a phone call yet so I can't speak for that, but the overall sound quality is very good. Similar to that of my much more expensive corded headphones. I'm not a sound guru by any means but I'm confident the average user would be pleased with these.

The only thing I'm not a huge fan of is that the headphones get a little warm after about an hour of use. Not quite "sweat pouring down my neck" hot, but noticeably warm. It became a nuisance after a while and I took them off. That only happened the once - after a longer period of use - so maybe it was a fluke, but it is worth noting. With small children around, I don't typically wear headphones longer than a half hour here or there so it's not an issue for me. Overall I really like the set and would definitely recommend them to friends.

I was able to purchase these headphones at a slight discount so that I could review them, but I did still buy them, and my opinions are genuine. It's a great pair of headphones - comfortable, stylish, and great quality. I'm very satisfied with my purchase!

Input: As a disclaimer, I'm not an audio snob, so take that as you will while reading my review. I'm really glad that I purchased these headphones. They are simple to use and provide very good sound. I bought these because I was not about to drop the $300 on the much more expensive Beats brand headphones who charge you more if you want wireless headphones. They are very comfy and fit on my ears decently. The only thing that slightly irritates me about the fit is that I have my ears pierced and even though I only wear studs, they make it kind of uncomfortable when wearing these headphones for a long time. Maybe that's just me. I use these with my iPhone, and my PC laptop and the headphones' Bluetooth capabilities are adequate. I have answered the phone while wearing these and the person on the other end was able to hear me loud and clear. The battery life is also excellent, and I've worn them for hours on end without the battery running out. I will say that if you are very particular about bass, or want a lot of bass, these are not the headphones for you. The sound quality is still good, but the bass is not loud and doesn't provide the same feeling you might want when you listen to a bass-heavy song. Overall, I'm satisfied with my purchase and would recommend them.

Input: This is a decent dash cam to have for any reason wheather you are using it for a dash cam just to save you if you get in an accident or you are using it to record just a day in the life type of video. It is decent for the money you will spend on it.

The camera itself: 5 out of 5 stars is very lightweight so you don't need to worry about it adding weight to anything like your rear view mirror. I was a little disappointed with the lightness to it just because it makes it feel cheap but once using it the weight did not bother me. I mean if it were heavy then you risk the rear view mirror falling. The plastic that it is made out of seems to be pretty decent, I haven't had any problems with it even on warm to hot days, all of the seams are very well put together no gaps or holes in it at all.

The screen: 4 out of 5 stars When I first turned on the camera in was in a different language so I had to figure out which setting was for the language to change it over to english. It wasn't that hard to figure out though the booklet helped me navigate so that I could change it back to the original. The screen is decent it definitely isn't the best of the best in display quality but it is only 2.7" so you really can't complain that much.

Video: Quality 4 out of 5 Stars The video record modes are great you can tweak a few features to make it better for you and what you are using is for. You can use it while driving in day or night. Which is great because not all accidents happen in the sunlight most happen at night when you least expect it. The night mode is not the best of video quality there is a smaller range due to the headlights and distance of which they reach, I mean it isn't that big of a problem but it doesn't allow you to record what happens before a vehicle hits you unless it is head on and you see them coming at you. The dat light recording is great it is in 1080P HD which is very decent quality. The video doesn't come out grainy or pixelated it is very clear and crisp you can make out things that are at a pretty far distance. I really like this camera mainly in day mode so that you can see everything.

Sound: Quality I would give it 3 out of 4 stars mainly because it sounds like you are in a tunnel or a barrel...I mean if you are recording for accident problems you really don't even need the sound feature unless you are speaking with a person that hit you or that you hit for insurance purposes. The sound isn't a huge issue because even though it is a tunnel sound or barrel ( just muffled sound like you have your finger half over the mic) you can still understand everything that is being said.

Software installed on the camera: 4 out of 5 stars. The software seems to be a little dated, I mean this is coming from a different country and is made for a different country so it isn't terrible at all it all responds well and with ease all the buttons when push respond very well. It just needs to be a little more updated so that it comes across the screen a little clearer.

All in all this get 4 out of 5 stars from me. I think that this is a decent dash cam to have for the price it is really a steal my only hint would be to use the correct wall plug in to charge the camera in the booklet it tells you the correct one to use. I used a different one the first time that I charged I didn't think that it would matter, but it did it only had about 30% after 45 minutes of charging so use the correct things with this camera. I have another dash cam and this one hooked to the bracket that I already had on my mirror this comes with a nice suction cup holder so you don't have to mount it on a permanent level and you can take it in and out of any vehicle which gives this camera an extra little bit of value to me.
I would highly recommend this little guy to anyone that is in the market for a dash cam.
I received this item at a discount for my opinion, others may vary depending on their own opinion of the product.
